item.title: Final Thoughts: Liverpool Clinch Huge Win Against Brighton
item.description: Final Thoughts: Liverpool Clinch Huge Win Against Brighton Liverpool 2–0 Brighton – Premier League Post-Match Report After a successful European win in midweek, the fifth-placed Reds returned to Premier League action at Anfield, welcoming Brighton to Merseyside for a challenging afternoon against a technically accomplished opponent. Liverpool emerged with all three points after a hard-fought 2–0 victory, scoring twice in a devastating four-minute spell during the opening half. Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak provided the goals, but this was ultimately a result built on resilience, defensive discipline and an ability to withstand sustained pressure. Moving to court in the table was very important. Brighton dominated possession for long periods, particularly after the break, but Liverpool defended their advantage impressively to secure another important league win under Andoni Iraola. item.content:encoded: Final Thoughts: Liverpool Clinch Huge Win Against Brighton Liverpool 2–0 Brighton – Premier League Post-Match Report After a successful European win in midweek, the fifth-placed Reds returned to Premier League action at Anfield, welcoming Brighton to Merseyside for a challenging afternoon against a technically accomplished opponent. Liverpool emerged with all three points after a hard-fought 2–0 victory, scoring twice in a devastating four-minute spell during the opening half. Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak provided the goals, but this was ultimately a result built on resilience, defensive discipline and an ability to withstand sustained pressure. Moving to court in the table was very important. Brighton dominated possession for long periods, particularly after the break, but Liverpool defended their advantage impressively to secure another important league win under Andoni Iraola. The Starting Eleven Liverpool XI GK – Alisson Becker RB – Ronald Araújo CB – Jérémy Jacquet CB – Virgil van Dijk (c) LB – Milos Kerkez CM – Ryan Gravenberch CM – Alexis Mac Allister RW – Cody Gakpo AM – Florian Wirtz LW – Bradley Barcola CF – Alexander Isak Substitutes Used Trey Nyoni → Florian Wirtz (64’) Lewis Koumas → Alexander Isak (76’) Rio Ngumoha → Bradley Barcola (76’) Kostas Tsimikas → Milos Kerkez (87’) Goals Liverpool 1–0 Brighton – Florian Wirtz – 17’ Liverpool 2–0 Brighton – Alexander Isak (Bradley Barcola) – 21’ Match Statistics Possession – Liverpool 36% | Brighton 64% xG – Liverpool 0.87 | Brighton 1.35 Total Shots – Liverpool 13 | Brighton 17 Shots on Target – Liverpool 4 | Brighton 1 Fouls – Liverpool 13 | Brighton 9 Corners – Liverpool 4 | Brighton 2 First Half Liverpool started with purpose, looking to use their pace and direct attacking options to exploit Brighton whenever space opened up. The visitors were always likely to enjoy spells of possession, but the Reds showed early intent and were rewarded with two goals in the space of four minutes. The breakthrough arrived in the 17th minute when Florian Wirtz found the net. The German’s effort gave Liverpool the lead and provided a platform for the hosts to build on their positive start. It was an important moment for Wirtz, who continues to offer creativity and quality between the lines. Four minutes later, Liverpool doubled their advantage. Bradley Barcola supplied the assist for Alexander Isak, who finished to make it 2–0. The quickfire goals gave Anfield a lift and left Brighton facing an uphill task despite their ability to control possession. Ronald Araújo was particularly impressive during the opening period. His strength and defensive awareness helped Liverpool manage Brighton’s attacking threat, while his willingness to drive forward offered an additional outlet. At the other end, Gakpo worked hard to connect Liverpool’s attacking play, and Barcola’s pace provided a constant threat. The two-goal cushion was an excellent reward for Liverpool’s efficiency. However, the underlying statistics suggested the visitors would have plenty of opportunities to respond. Brighton were capable of moving the ball patiently and finding spaces, meaning Liverpool needed to remain disciplined rather than simply sit back and invite pressure. Second Half Brighton took greater control after the interval, enjoying the majority of possession and pushing Liverpool deeper into their own half. The visitors finished the match with 64% of the ball and 17 attempts, compared with Liverpool’s 13, and their territorial dominance was particularly evident during the second half. The Reds were forced to demonstrate a different side of their game. Rather than dictate proceedings through possession, they needed to defend their penalty area, stay compact and limit Brighton’s opportunities to find a route back into the contest. Alisson Becker was composed throughout, while Van Dijk and Jacquet provided important defensive leadership and organisation. Araújo continued to impress, using his physicality to deal with Brighton’s advances and helping Liverpool maintain their shape under pressure. Despite Brighton’s territorial advantage, Liverpool restricted them to just one shot on target. Their expected-goals figure of 1.35 showed that the visitors created opportunities, but the home side’s defensive resilience prevented that pressure from translating into a goal. Iraola made his first change in the 64th minute, introducing Trey Nyoni for Wirtz to provide a different midfield option. Further changes followed in the 76th minute, with Lewis Koumas replacing Isak and Rio Ngumoha coming on for Barcola. Kostas Tsimikas replaced Kerkez in the 87th minute as Liverpool looked to see out the closing stages. The second half was not about Liverpool dominating the ball or creating a succession of chances. It was about managing the situation, remaining organised and refusing to allow Brighton back into the game. The Reds achieved exactly that, protecting their early lead until the final whistle. Final Thoughts This was a hard-fought victory that demonstrated Liverpool’s growing resilience under Iraola. The opening 21 minutes provided the goals, but the remaining period demanded concentration, discipline and a willingness to suffer without the ball. Brighton were territorially dominant after the break, and Liverpool will recognise that there are areas to improve. Their 36% possession and 0.87 expected goals show that this was not an attacking performance built on sustained control. However, football is ultimately about taking opportunities and defending your advantage, and the Reds did both effectively. Wirtz and Isak delivered the decisive moments, Barcola provided the assist for the second goal, and Araújo was outstanding at both ends. The defensive unit also deserves considerable credit for limiting Brighton to one shot on target despite facing 17 attempts. Liverpool’s resilience is becoming an impressive feature of their recent performances. They have shown that they can recover from difficult situations, as demonstrated against Villarreal, and now they have produced a different kind of victory by protecting an early lead under sustained pressure. My pre-match prediction was Liverpool 2–1 Brighton. The Reds kept a clean sheet and secured a 2–0 win, making this another valuable result in their pursuit of consistency. There is still room for improvement, but the ability to win matches in different ways is an encouraging sign for Iraola’s side. Steven Smith’s Pre-Match Prediction: Liverpool 2–1 Brighton

item.title: Mou's Midfield Puzzle! Boss explains why Bernardo Silva holds key to Real Madrid balance
item.description: FBL-ESP-LIGA-BARCELONA-REAL MADRID - AFP Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho discussed the integration of summer signing Bernardo Silva following their 2-1 El Clasico victory. Mourinho explained how blending different midfield profiles provides Los Blancos with superior tactical balance. Mourinho manages midfielder workloads at Camp Nou Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho highlighted squad depth and tactical midfield combinations following a hard-fought 2-1 El Clasico victory over Barcelona. Summer arrival Bernardo Silva started in central midfield, working tirelessly for 75 minutes before being replaced by Eduardo Camavinga. Camavinga went on to assist Kylian Mbappe's 88th-minute match-winner. Mourinho emphasized that every member of his deep roster must remain ready to impact games. Manager details Bernardo Silva's integration process Mourinho offered a clear assessment of Bernardo's ongoing adaptation to Real Madrid's team dynamic. "Regarding Bernardo’s situation, I’ve said that he’s been here for a little over three months," Mourinho noted. "Obviously, I know him very well, but knowing someone very well is one thing, and seeing how he can integrate into the team dynamic is another." "The group is very strong. I’ll never tell you, ‘This is my starting eleven’... everyone works very hard," he asserted. Tactical balance demands specific midfield profiles Mourinho explained his preference for mixing tactical characteristics rather than deploying identical profiles together in central midfield. "I’ve learned that in midfield, having a combination of talents gives us more than having two players with similar characteristics," Mourinho revealed. "This means that I don’t use the double pivot of Bernardo with Guler, or only in desperate situations." "I prefer this combination of talents, which gives us balance when defending and more quality when launching attacks," he added. Real Madrid options keep title rivals guessing Mourinho's tactical flexibility allows Real Madrid to adapt smoothly depending on opponent setups and match contexts. With Bernardo, Camavinga, Guler, and Tchouameni vying for spots, midfield competition remains high. Real Madrid turn their attention to Santander in their next La Liga test.

item.title: Nick Wright has ‘old school’ reaction to Chiefs getting dominated by Seahawks
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Nick Wright did not hold back after the Kansas City Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the 2026 NFL season, with the Fox Sports analyst describing their 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks as an “old school a** whupping”. The Chiefs entered the contest unbeaten but struggled to find any rhythm against the reigning Super Bowl champions, who controlled the game on both sides of the ball. Seattle’s victory was led by wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who recorded 150 receiving yards and a touchdown as the Seahawks improved to 4-3. Nick Wright reacts as Seattle Seahawks dominate Kansas City Chiefs in 20-3 win Wright shared his reaction on X after watching Kansas City endure a difficult night, making it clear that he felt the Seahawks had been superior throughout the contest. “Old school a** whupping by the champs tonight. They dominated in every phase of the game,” he wrote. The result was a statement performance from Seattle, whose defence limited Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs to just three points. Kansas City managed only 213 total yards, including 50 on the ground. Mahomes finished with 165 passing yards and an interception, while the Seahawks also kept Kenneth Walker III quiet after the running back joined Kansas City in the off-season. Walker managed just 36 yards from 14 carries against his former team, a significant drop from the league-leading 133 rushing yards per game he had averaged entering the contest. Meanwhile, Smith-Njigba proved difficult to contain. The receiver caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, while quarterback Sam Darnold threw for 257 yards and a score. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid accepted responsibility for the disappointing performance, admitting that his team struggled in all three phases. “Listen, all three phases we struggled, so we’ve got to do better, and that’s my responsibility,” Reid said. “So I take full responsibility for this. We’ve got to play better as a team.” Kansas City will now look to respond against the Denver Broncos, while Seattle will aim to build on a victory that showed why the defending champions remain a formidable opponent. item.title: What Lakers’ Luka Doncic told Walker Kessler after big man’s struggles vs. Jazz
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images What Lakers’ Luka Doncic told Walker Kessler after big man’s struggles vs. Jazz appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Walker Kessler had a bit of a rough homecoming on Sunday afternoon as he faced the Utah Jazz in Salt Lake City for the first time as a member of the Los Angeles Lakers . After starring in the Lakers’ first two games of the season, Kessler’s production fell off in his third game of the campaign, finishing with just two points, seven rebounds, and one block in 28 minutes of play. The Lakers did mount a furious comeback and defeat the Jazz, 132-123, so in the end, it’s not like Kessler’s poor night doomed his team. But of course, this is a far cry from the kind of game the Purple and Gold need him to have on a nightly basis. But in true team fashion, Lakers star Luka Doncic simply reassured Kessler that they have his back and he just needs to shrug off this substandard performance. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Obviously it wasn’t his best game. But we won the game and he had two fantastic first games. I told him just move on, we won this game and we got your back,” Doncic said in his postgame presser, via Khobi Price of the California Post. Luka’s message to Walker Kessler after his struggles tonight: “Obviously it wasn’t his best game. But we won the game and he had two fantastic first games. I told him just move on, we won this game and we got your back.” (Via: @khobi_price ) pic.twitter.com/5cpL1REABs — LakersCenter (@LALakersCenter) October 26, 2026 Kessler averaged 24 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.5 steals, and 4.0 blocks through his first two games for the Lakers, which were wins against the Golden State Warriors and Los Angeles Clippers, respectively. One would have thought that a matchup against the Jazz would be another opportunity for him to feast . After all, Jusuf Nurkic is out and the Jazz are starting Jaren Jackson Jr. at center, which isn’t his natural position. But Kessler did admit that his emotions were too much to handle , and the Lakers did pick up the slack in the end. Doncic, in particular, went off for 52 points, eight rebounds, and 10 assists, and the Lakers have now moved to 3-0 on the season. Related: Lakers’ Walker Kessler gets 100% real on cooling off against Jazz Related: Luka Doncic’s response to Kendrick Perkins after 52-point eruption goes viral

item.title: Francesco Bagnaia: MotoGP riders not consulted over Australian GP cancellation
item.description: Motorsport photo Francesco Bagnaia has revealed that MotoGP riders were not consulted before the championship cancelled Sunday’s Australian Grand Prix at Phillip Island, but said they had to respect the decision because safety was at stake. The iconic Australian circuit was unable to give MotoGP a proper racing farewell due to the adverse weather conditions. After several delays, the weekend’s full-distance race was cancelled because of the heavy rain and strong winds affecting the visibility. Visibility never improved sufficiently to allow racing to resume, and the decision was eventually taken to cancel the on-track action. According to Bagnaia, the championship made the call without consulting the riders. The Ducati rider spoke to UK MotoGP broadcaster TNT Sports after Sunday's cancellation was confirmed. Asked whether the riders had been given a say in the decision, Bagnaia replied: “No.” However, the Italian made it clear that riders had to respect the decision because their safety was at stake. "But in these kind of situations, we need to respect the decisions [of the organisers],” the three-time world champion said. Nevertheless, Bagnaia admitted that he would have liked to race. “Yes, absolutely,” he said. "It’s clear that the conditions were a bit tricky and very cold, but we have raced in worse conditions than this. “It’s a shame to have this kind of Sunday, to remain in the garage in a track like this, the last time [MotoGP visited Phillip Island]. "I just hope that in the future we can come back to [Phillip Island to] enjoy because like we saw yesterday, the races produced at this track are amazing; great battles." Pitlane de Phillip Island con lluvia Pitlane de Phillip Island con lluvia With the race cancelled, riders took to the track behind the Safety Car for a couple of demonstration laps to bid farewell to the venue and acknowledge the fans, who had been expected to fill the grandstands for a historic final day of MotoGP racing at Phillip Island. The poor weather made its presence felt from early on Sunday morning, forcing delays and the cancellation of scheduled sessions as the day progressed. It was explained from the outset that the race was not cancelled because of the condition of the track itself, but because poor visibility prevented the medical helicopter from flying safely. MotoGP race director Graham Webber explained that a one-hour window was required for a flight from Phillip Island to Melbourne, where the designated hospital is located, in the event that a rider needed to be evacuated following a serious accident. The helicopter was essential because the journey could not be made by road within the required timeframe, with an ambulance taking more than 45 minutes to travel between the two locations. item.title: Texans’ Jaylin Noel injury update puts further damper on Giants loss
item.description: Texans’ Jaylin Noel injury update puts further damper on Giants loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans failed to extend their winning streak in Week 7, suffering a 27-21 loss against the New York Giants. Additionally, Jaylin Noel’s injury made the loss even more frustrating for Houston, and the latest update on the wide receiver’s condition has raised further concerns. After the game, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed that Noel had suffered a turf toe injury and was still undergoing evaluation. “DeMeco Ryans said Jaylin Noel has a turf toe injury, which is why he didn’t return. He’s wearing a boot,” Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Texans reported. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Noel sustained the injury during a kickoff return in the fourth quarter against New York, forcing him to exit the game early. He finished with two receptions on two targets for minus-three receiving yards. The Texans star also contributed on special teams, returning a kickoff for 21 yards and recording an 11-yard punt return before his afternoon came to an end. The Houston team struggled to get their receiving corps going throughout the game. Nico Collins managed just two receptions for six yards, while Noel’s early departure further limited Houston’s options in the passing game. Though the Texans managed to force overtime, their offensive struggles ultimately proved costly as they failed to secure the victory. The injury was particularly disappointing because Noel had shown encouraging signs in the previous game. He recorded 107 receiving yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6. Houston’s upcoming bye week could provide Noel with valuable recovery time. The Texans will have an additional week to evaluate the injury and determine whether the receiver can return without aggravating the problem. However, turf toe injuries can vary in severity. Hence, his recovery timeline will depend on the results of further evaluation. The loss dropped Houston to 2-5, while the Giants improved to 4-2-1 heading into their bye week . Related: Texans most to blame for brutal home loss to JJ McCarthy’s Giants Related: DeMeco Ryans rips ‘ridiculous’ penalty woes that keep costing Texans games

Nico Collins managed just two receptions for six yards, while Noel’s early departure further limited Houston’s options in the passing game. Though the Texans managed to force overtime, their offensive struggles ultimately proved costly as they failed to secure the victory. The injury was particularly disappointing because Noel had shown encouraging signs in the previous game. He recorded 107 receiving yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6. Houston’s upcoming bye week could provide Noel with valuable recovery time. The Texans will have an additional week to evaluate the injury and determine whether the receiver can return without aggravating the problem. However, turf toe injuries can vary in severity. Hence, his recovery timeline will depend on the results of further evaluation. The loss dropped Houston to 2-5, while the Giants improved to 4-2-1 heading into their bye week . item.title: More trouble for Barcelona as key defender goes out injured against Real Madrid
item.description: More trouble for Barcelona as key defender goes out injured against Real Madrid Barcelona suffered another injury setback during their 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid , with Xavi Espart forced off in the 29th minute of the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season. The young defender had started at Spotify Camp Nou but was unable to continue after experiencing increasing discomfort, leaving Hansi Flick facing further uncertainty over his defensive options. Alejandro Balde replaced Espart, while Joao Cancelo moved across to right-back. Barcelona must now await medical tests to determine the extent of Espart’s injury and how long the academy graduate could be unavailable. Xavi Espart forced off after struggling with discomfort Espart had made a promising start to the match before his physical problems became impossible to ignore. The defender had already experienced discomfort in his soleus muscle during the week leading up to El Clasico and received an injection before the game to help him play. His condition appeared to worsen following contact with Real Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni earlier in the match. Although Espart attempted to continue, he struggled with the discomfort and eventually went to ground after trying to chase Yan Diomande. The Barcelona coaching staff subsequently decided to withdraw him rather than risk aggravating the problem. Espart left the pitch to applause from the home supporters, having shown his determination to remain involved despite his difficulties. The exact nature and severity of the injury remain unclear, with further medical examinations required before Barcelona can establish a recovery timeline. Balde replaces Espart as Flick reshuffles defence Flick reacted to Espart’s withdrawal by introducing Balde, who had seen limited playing time during the season despite featuring in Barcelona’s Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain. The substitution prompted a defensive reshuffle, with Balde taking the left-back position and Cancelo moving to his natural role on the right. The adjustment gave Barcelona an experienced alternative but disrupted the defensive setup Flick had selected for the Clasico. Espart’s absence is particularly frustrating given the progress he has made this season. His display against PSG in Paris further strengthened his reputation as one of Barcelona’s emerging defensive talents. Barcelona face growing defensive injury concerns Espart’s injury adds to an increasingly difficult situation for Flick, with Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Roony Bardghji also on Barcelona’s injury list, according to the supplied report. The growing number of absentees threatens to limit Flick’s ability to rotate his defence during a demanding period of the season. Espart had taken advantage of his opportunities to establish himself in the first team, making the latest setback particularly disappointing for the youngster.

item.title: Real Madrid goalkeeper Andriy Lunin makes El Clasico history after Barcelona victory
item.description: Real Madrid goalkeeper Andriy Lunin makes El Clasico history after Barcelona victory Real Madrid travelled to Barcelona knowing full well that a victory could take them closer to the Catalan giants in the La Liga title race. Los Blancos were dealt a very late blow , as it emerged that Thibaut Courtois was down with the flu and could not feature against Barça . Andriy Lunin was forced to start the big game, and he passed the test with flying colours, helping his team secure a 2-1 victory over Barça . The Ukrainian made history, becoming the first goalkeeper to win at least four of his first five El Clasico appearances . He entered the encounter with three victories and one defeat against the Catalans, but his latest appearance at the Spotify Camp Nou took that record to four wins in five matches. Lunin makes history in El Clasico It was Lunin’s first competitive appearance of the season, making the challenge even greater. Despite his lack of recent match action, the 27-year-old produced an assured performance against Barcelona. His most important intervention came in the 66th minute, when he made an outstanding one-handed save to deny Gerard Martin’s header. The stop proved crucial, keeping Madrid level after Raphinha had cancelled out Kylian Mbappe’s first-half opener. Mbappe eventually scored the winner late in the second half, securing three valuable points for Mourinho’s side. Lunin proves his value to Real Madrid Lunin’s record against Barcelona now includes victories in October 2022, January 2024, April 2024 and October 2026. His only defeat came in October 2024, when Madrid suffered a 4-0 loss at the Santiago Bernabeu. Kylian Mbappe scored the eventual winner for Real Madrid against Barcelona. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) His latest performance also reinforces why Los Blancos are better off with a reliable alternative to Thibaut Courtois who can step in whenever needed. Goalkeepers who spend long periods on the bench face a difficult task when suddenly called upon for major fixtures. Lunin showed that he can handle that responsibility, combining concentration with decisive shot-stopping when Madrid needed him most. Although Courtois remains the established first choice, Madrid have a goalkeeper capable of delivering in demanding circumstances. Lunin’s impressive El Clasico record is a fitting reward for his patience, and he will hope to take such chances whenever they present themselves in the future.

item.title: (Video) Two Ronald Araujo moments at Anfield on Sunday show why he’s adored by Liverpool fans
item.description: (Video) Two Ronald Araujo moments at Anfield on Sunday show why he’s adored by Liverpool fans If Liverpool’s win over Villarreal last week was Rio Ngumoha’s night, then the 2-0 victory against Brighton on Sunday was the Ronald Araujo show. The Uruguayan has swiftly endeared himself to Kopites for his all-action performances, and he further strengthened his bond with supporters by leaping into the Anfield Road Stand to celebrate his equaliser against the LaLiga side six days ago. His wholehearted and composed displays have already led to some pundits reversing their negative opinions of him when he joined on loan from Barcelona in August, and his reputation as a fans’ favourite was embellished by two moments in particular yesterday. (Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) Araujo brilliance summed up by two moments Liverpool were two goals to the good by the 21st minute on Sunday, but Brighton began to worry the home side towards the end of the first half. At one point, Maxim De Cuyper attempted to dribble past Araujo when the defender was lying down on the ground, but the Uruguay international nudged the ball away from the Seagulls player with his head whilst on the turf in an attempt to clear the danger. Then, with 10 minutes of normal time remaining and the visitors applying sustained pressure in the hope of triggering a late comeback, Malick Yalcouye was charging along the left flank until being stopped in his tracks by a thundering challenge from the Reds’ number 33, who got to the ball as the Brighton substitute jumped to avoid him. Araujo is already idolised at Anfield Araujo’s name booming around Anfield after that 81st-minute challenge told you everything about the esteem in which he’s already held by Liverpool fans after just 12 appearances for the club. The Uruguayan feels like a throwback to a different era when defenders were preoccupied by doing their job by any means necessary rather than trying to look neat and tidy, although it’d be disingenuous to label him a mere flat-track bully. The 27-year-old is also a very good footballer – he wouldn’t have played for Barcelona and Liverpool if he weren’t – and while other right-backs might have a greater attacking instinct, his presence unquestionably makes the back four stronger. Araujo was throwing himself into challenges yesterday as though the loss of a clean sheet would be a major personal affront, and the prevailing opinion among many Reds supporters is that the club should waste no time in trying to convert his loan move into a permanent transfer. If it felt as though there was a disconnect between players and fans towards the end of last season, then the Uruguay colossus has done plenty to re-establish that crucial sense of harmony between those on the pitch and in the stands.

item.title: Antonelli delivers 'the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet'
item.description: Kimi Antonelli needs two points in Mexico to be certain of becoming world champion [PA Media] The race that took Kimi Antonelli to the brink of a record-breaking world championship was, in the words of his Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff, "the best he has delivered so far" and "the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet". Not yet. Not quite. But so very near. The 20-year-old Italian's victory in the United States Grand Prix puts him in an impregnable position. Antonelli is so far ahead in the points that the only way he could not win the title in Mexico City next weekend is if either his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton win the race. Even then, Antonelli will guarantee the title if he finishes ninth, or 10th if it's Hamilton. He arrived here thanks to one of the most dominant victories of the season, in a car in which Russell could finish only eighth, albeit hampered by a five-second penalty. While Russell was toiling and failing to pass McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Antonelli was operating on another level entirely, as he has so often this season. "Exceptional," Wolff said, "and I think he's outperformed the car." Antonelli wins in US but has to wait to secure title Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings Antonelli came to Austin already in a strong position in the championship, knowing he would clinch the title if he won with Russell finishing lower than eighth and Hamilton lower than fourth. He achieved his part of the bargain but Russell and Hamilton did just enough to keep things alive until this coming weekend. Russell was eighth and Hamilton fourth. Some drivers tighten up when they get this close to achieving their lifetime's ambition. Not Antonelli. He said he was going to treat this like any other weekend, but it wasn't just talk. It's exactly what he did. "He comes in," Wolff told BBC Sport after the race, in a conversation after finishing his official news conference, "sits on my chair, feet up, and keeps chatting away and saying: 'This is so funny. I'm not thinking about the championship at all.' And in a kind of youngish excitement, almost like it's surreal. And that's why it's not so important." Did Wolff think that was because Antonelli's lead was so large that he had no need to feel any pressure, or was it innate? "The advantage helps," he said. "But it's also innate in him and I don't think that it's something to be trained for. He's not over-thinking it." Wolff's claim about this being Antonelli's best performance so far might surprise anyone who watched him win his home grand prix at Monza from 19th on the grid. When this was pointed out, Wolff replied: "My problem is that I don't remember past races. So now you're saying Monza was actually also pretty good, obviously with the advantage of the home crowd and seeing all these tifosi that were a little bit confused, wearing red, and an Italian with the Mercedes outfit up on the podium. And I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Merc
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli needs two points in Mexico to be certain of becoming world champion [PA Media] The race that took Kimi Antonelli to the brink of a record-breaking world championship was, in the words of his Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff, "the best he has delivered so far" and "the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet". Not yet. Not quite. But so very near. The 20-year-old Italian's victory in the United States Grand Prix puts him in an impregnable position. Antonelli is so far ahead in the points that the only way he could not win the title in Mexico City next weekend is if either his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton win the race. Even then, Antonelli will guarantee the title if he finishes ninth, or 10th if it's Hamilton. He arrived here thanks to one of the most dominant victories of the season, in a car in which Russell could finish only eighth, albeit hampered by a five-second penalty. While Russell was toiling and failing to pass McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Antonelli was operating on another level entirely, as he has so often this season. "Exceptional," Wolff said, "and I think he's outperformed the car." Antonelli wins in US but has to wait to secure title Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings Antonelli came to Austin already in a strong position in the championship, knowing he would clinch the title if he won with Russell finishing lower than eighth and Hamilton lower than fourth. He achieved his part of the bargain but Russell and Hamilton did just enough to keep things alive until this coming weekend. Russell was eighth and Hamilton fourth. Some drivers tighten up when they get this close to achieving their lifetime's ambition. Not Antonelli. He said he was going to treat this like any other weekend, but it wasn't just talk. It's exactly what he did. "He comes in," Wolff told BBC Sport after the race, in a conversation after finishing his official news conference, "sits on my chair, feet up, and keeps chatting away and saying: 'This is so funny. I'm not thinking about the championship at all.' And in a kind of youngish excitement, almost like it's surreal. And that's why it's not so important." Did Wolff think that was because Antonelli's lead was so large that he had no need to feel any pressure, or was it innate? "The advantage helps," he said. "But it's also innate in him and I don't think that it's something to be trained for. He's not over-thinking it." Wolff's claim about this being Antonelli's best performance so far might surprise anyone who watched him win his home grand prix at Monza from 19th on the grid. When this was pointed out, Wolff replied: "My problem is that I don't remember past races. So now you're saying Monza was actually also pretty good, obviously with the advantage of the home crowd and seeing all these tifosi that were a little bit confused, wearing red, and an Italian with the Mercedes outfit up on the podium. And I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Mercedes caps next year. "So both of them were pretty good. But the headline that this is the best we can keep." Antonelli agreed. "Monza, we clearly had the fastest car," he said. "We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back. But it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick. "Definitely, Monza was a super-special one, and one that I will remember forever. But this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good." Mercedes went to Austin with both cars in the new upgraded specification that had proved unconvincing, to say the least, when it made its debut in Malaysia two races ago. There, Wolff said he thought it had made the car 0.3secs per lap slower. The team split the cars in Singapore to try to understand the package better, and then used it on both cars in Austin. Antonelli stuck it on pole and dominated the race. Russell's performance looked more like the one the car produced in Malaysia. "The update we put on the car is difficult to operate," Wolff said. "And Kimi landed it. "Maybe it's a bit harsh to say but I think his driving style just glues with the car. We saw that in qualifying yesterday where on his last lap he could have been another 0.15-0.2 secs up. And on the other side George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult." Alberto Ascari is the last Italian to win the F1 drivers' championship, in 1952 and 1953 [Getty Images] When Antonelli clinches the title, he will become the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari in 1953. It's a remarkable statistic for a country which is so engrained in the sport, and it certainly resonates with his compatriots. McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "As an Italian, wow, we need to go back to Ascari, the names that they created the inspiration for all of us. To see an Italian achieving this level of performance and results in Formula 1, that's particularly thrilling, as an Italian person in motorsport." Stella's answer continued into an area that begins to explain the way in which he has proved so superior to Russell this year. "Going more into the technical, and specifically this season, Kimi is a very interesting one to look at, because he pretty much attacks all the times," Stella said. "You see how often he's just going off track, and you see his onboard (camera), he's pretty aggressive. But at the same time, this seems to be not only kind of an aggressive driving, or an attacking driving, but effective. "And if we think how much we talk in these media sessions about the cars being difficult to drive consistently fast, it should be recognised how much he's been able to harness his driving style with what is required of the cars. "But at the same time, almost contradicting what I'm saying, when is the time to bring home the result, he's been able to do it. "So he's the deserving leader of this championship. He's writing an important piece of history for motorsport, because once he achieves the championship, he will be the youngest." Antonelli will beat by more than three years the previous record for youngest winner of the championship, Sebastian Vettel in 2010. As with the title itself, he is aware of the forthcoming achievement, but not letting it affect him. "I'm going to approach it with the same mindset," he said. "Just trying to have as much fun as possible, trying to hopefully fight for another win. "It would be best to finish on a high, and that's the goal. But I'm just going to try to enjoy the rest of the season from now on." item.title: Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings
item.description: Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc were first and second at the US Grand Prix [Getty Images] Championship leader Kimi Antonelli sealed his ninth victory of the season with victory at the United States Grand Prix in Austin. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was second and Red Bull's Max Verstappen third. Mercedes' Antonelli, 20, can become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history if he finishes ninth or higher at the Mexico City Grand Prix next weekend. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Texas. Kimi Antonelli - 10/10 A superb weekend under the added pressure of having his first opportunity to seal the championship. Produced an outstanding lap for pole and then controlled the race beautifully, making the one-stop work while many around him needed two. Charles Leclerc - 9.5/10 Very close to a perfect weekend himself. Fastest in both Friday practice sessions, qualified fourth and then raced brilliantly in his Ferrari to second, including late passes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen. Max Verstappen - 8.5/10 Quick all weekend and put the Red Bull on the front row, but the poor start immediately made his race more difficult. Recovered well despite problems with the car and still came away with a sixth consecutive podium. Lewis Hamilton - 7.5/10 Another strong weekend but behind team-mate Leclerc for the majority of it. Fastest in final practice, only narrowly behind Leclerc in qualifying and fought his way back to fourth after Ferrari committed to the two-stop strategy. Lando Norris - 8/10 Recovered well from eighth on the grid but qualifying should have been better as his quickest Q3 lap was deleted for track limits. McLaren's decision to leave him out on ageing tyres cost him late on, so fifth was not entirely of his own making. Isack Hadjar - 8.5/10 An excellent turnaround after struggling badly with the Red Bull during practice. Qualified a superb third, ran strongly in the race and eventually finished sixth despite throttle mapping problems and moving aside for team-mate Verstappen. Oscar Piastri - 6.5/10 A fairly subdued weekend by the McLaren man's standards. Seventh in qualifying and seventh in the race, although the first-lap battle with George Russell went against him and the stewards decided the Mercedes driver was at fault. George Russell - 5.5/10 A disappointing weekend given what the other Mercedes achieved. Admitted both of his Q3 laps were poor and then picked up a five-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in his battle with Piastri, eventually finishing eighth. Liam Lawson - 8/10 Another quietly excellent weekend from Lawson. Racing Bulls sacrificed a proper Q3 attempt to preserve tyres for Sunday and he converted ninth on the grid into ninth at the finish to score again. Pierre Gasly - 8/10 Probably extracted just about everything available from the Alpine. Missed Q3 but fought his way back into the points after an early dice with Haas' Oliver Bearman. Antonelli

Oscar Piastri - 6.5/10 A fairly subdued weekend by the McLaren man's standards. George Russell - 5.5/10 A disappointing weekend given what the other Mercedes achieved. Liam Lawson - 8/10 Another quietly excellent weekend from Lawson. Racing Bulls sacrificed a proper Q3 attempt to preserve tyres for Sunday and he converted ninth on the grid into ninth at the finish to score again. Pierre Gasly - 8/10 Probably extracted just about everything available from the Alpine. Missed Q3 but fought his way back into the points after an early dice with Haas' Oliver Bearman. Antonelli wins in US but has to wait to secure title Antonelli delivers 'the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet' Nico Hulkenberg- 7/10 Another solid if unspectacular weekend for the Audi driver. Just missed Q3 and spent Sunday on the fringes of the points before eventually finishing 11th. Arvid Lindblad - 7.5/10 Reaching Q3 was an excellent effort after admitting team-mate Lawson had been quicker than him for much of the weekend. A power-unit penalty dropped him from ninth to 14th on the grid and he recovered a couple of positions to 12th. Gabriel Bortoleto - 8/10 A much better weekend than 13th suggests. Produced what he described as one of his best qualifying laps before helping team-mate Hulkenberg with a tow, then recovered from 21st on the grid after an enormous power-unit penalty. Esteban Ocon - 6/10 Out in Q1 and again lacked the pace team-mate Bearman had shown earlier in the weekend. Gained places at the start and Haas eventually prioritised his undamaged car, but 14th was all he could manage. Lance Stroll - 6/10 Started from the pit lane after Aston Martin made changes to the car and fitted additional power unit components, so 15th represented a reasonable recovery. Beat team-mate Fernando Alonso to the flag after a weekend where neither car looked particularly competitive. Fernando Alonso - 6.5/10 Getting the Aston Martin into Q2 was encouraging and penalties initially promoted him to 12th on the grid. But he went backwards on Sunday and contact with Williams' Alex Albon didn't help as he eventually finished behind Stroll after a slow pit stop. Alex Albon - 5.5/10 Williams knew this circuit would expose the weaknesses of their car and that proved to be the case. Qualified behind team-mate Carlos Sainz but at least he recovered to lead the team home after an eventful opening part of the race. Carlos Sainz - 5/10 A mistake late in his final qualifying lap contributed to a Q1 exit on a weekend when Williams were already struggling badly. Finished behind Albon and never looked capable of rescuing points from a difficult weekend. Sergio Perez - 4.5/10 Beat team-mate Valtteri Bottas in qualifying despite suffering an energy-recovery issue on his final lap. But Cadillac simply didn't have competitive pace at their home race, and P19 was a fairly anonymous result. Valtteri Bottas - 4/10 Qualified last before eventually retiring late enough to trigger the final virtual safety car. There wasn't much evidence across the weekend that Cadillac had the performance to achieve anything significant. Franco Colapinto - 6/10 Qualified 14th but a 10-place power-unit penalty left the Alpine driver effectively starting from the back. His retirement meant there was little opportunity to turn the weekend around. Oliver Bearman - 5/10 There had been real promise after he led Haas throughout Friday and initially looked quick enough for 13th in qualifying before losing his lap to track limits. Sunday unravelled with contact, a penalty and damage before he eventually retired. item.title: How to follow Mexico City Grand Prix on the BBC
item.description: The Mexico City Grand Prix signed a contract extension last year to stay on the F1 calendar until 2028 [Getty Images] Round 19 of the 2026 Formula 1 season heads to the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez for the Mexico City Grand Prix, from 30 October to 1 November. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli sealed victory from pole position last time out in the United States, and was joined on the podium by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen. The 20-year-old Italian is now 123 points clear of team-mate George Russell in the drivers' standings, and will make history in Mexico as the youngest F1 world champion if he finishes ninth or better. If Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not win the race, Antonelli will lift the title wherever he finishes. Lights out for Sunday's 71-lap race is at 20:00 GMT. Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings Antonelli delivers 'the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet' Session start times and BBC coverage Commentary of the weekend will be available across BBC Radio 5 Live, 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app. You can also ask your smart speaker to "play 5 Live", for example. Make sure to listen to every episode of the Chequered Flag podcast. For the first time this year, the post-race show for every grand prix is available to watch on BBC iPlayer and YouTube. All times GMT Friday, 30 October First practice: 18:30-19:30 - 5 Sports Extra Second practice: 22:00-23:00 - 5 Sports Extra Saturday, 31 October Third practice: 17:30-18:30 - 5 Sports Extra Qualifying: 21:00-22:00 - 5 Sports Extra Sunday, 1 November Race: 20:00 - 5 Live World champion Lando Norris took a dominant win in Mexico City last year, with Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen also on the podium [Getty Images] What is the Mexico City weather forecast? The early forecast suggests it will be a warm weekend in the Mexican capital, but Friday's practice sessions could see some light rain. For Sunday's race, which starts at 2pm local time, conditions should be dry with a high temperatures of 24C. Andrew Benson Q&A: Send us your questions

item.title: Pennant has more than 50 stitches after dog attack
item.description: Jermaine Pennant made 341 professional appearances [Getty Images] Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant says he needed more than 50 stitches after being mauled by a dog. The 43-year-old was walking his two dogs in north London last week when he was attacked by a German Shepherd. The former Liverpool and Stoke City winger said the dog latched on to his leg and refused to let go as he tried to protect his own dog, King. King then intervened to help fight off the attacking dog, preventing "what could've been an horrendous situation", Pennant said in a post on Instagram. Pennant told the Sun he required more than 50 stitches to his right leg after sustaining four bite wounds in the attack and receiving hospital treatment. He added that King was unhurt, but did not give details about the German Shepherd. He said he declined to report the attack to police. "So I was attacked by a German shepherd, I tried to protect King but the dog got my leg, I was on the floor with the dog still attached with no sign of letting go, until King intervened as he didn't know what was going on," said Pennant. "But the minute he did he fought the dog off and saved what could've been a horrendous situation for me. "King was unhurt with a little nip on his leg, but had blood covered all over him which wasn't mine. At this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn't King's." The picture uploaded to Instagram shows Pennant with a bandage on his leg alongside King on a sofa, while he also thanked his partner Mimmi Montgomery for looking after them. "My hero still protecting me and trying to look after me. King you're a legend, love you, man's best friend. Thanks Mimmi Montgomery for taking care of us both." Pennant, who is a pundit for Talksport, made 231 Premier League appearances in a 19-year career before retiring in 2018. item.title: Denis Bouanga and Leo Walta rescue LAFC in El Trafico thriller to secure MLS Cup playoff spot
item.description: LA Galaxy v Los Angeles Football Club - Getty Images Sport LAFC secured their place in the MLS Cup Playoffs following a dramatic 2-2 draw against rivals LA Galaxy. Interim boss Xavi Tamarit praised his side's resilience as Denis Bouanga inspired a stunning second-half comeback after falling two goals behind in El Trafico. LAFC secure playoff spot in derby thriller LAFC have booked their place in the MLS Cup Playoffs following a thrilling 2-2 draw with the LA Galaxy at BMO Stadium. The hosts fought back from a two-goal deficit to salvage a crucial point in the latest edition of El Trafico. Joseph Paintsil had put the Galaxy in complete control after capitalising on defensive errors to score twice. However, LAFC responded immediately with a quickfire double to rescue their postseason ambitions. The result guarantees LAFC a fifth consecutive playoff appearance. It also marks their eighth postseason qualification in just nine seasons. Tamarit praises dramatic second-half fightback Interim head coach Tamarit was thrilled by the fighting spirit shown by his players. His team had dominated stretches of the first half but found themselves trailing before conceding again early in the second. Despite the defensive setbacks, the hosts rallied impressively to rescue the match. "I am very proud about the team, how we overcame in a really difficult situation that we didn't deserve," Tamarit told reporters. "They never give up." The comeback was sparked by Bouanga, who pounced on a rebound after Galaxy goalkeeper JT Marcinkowski spilled Armindo Sieb's shot. Leo Walta then levelled the match following a dangerous cross from Heung-min Son. Defensive errors frustrate LAFC squad While the comeback was commendable, LAFC were left frustrated by the manner of the goals they conceded. Paintsil’s second strike came after Hugo Lloris spilled a shot from Erik Thommy, highlighting their defensive frailties. Defender Aaron Long was critical of the backline, describing both Galaxy goals as "a little cheap, a little easy." He added: "Scoring two goals at home, that should be a win." Pushing for a home playoff advantage LAFC will now turn their attention to securing a higher seed with just two regular-season matches remaining. A strong finish is essential if they are to earn a coveted home fixture in the upcoming playoffs. In their final two matches, LAFC will face Minnesota United on November 2, and then, six days later, they will travel to take on the Seattle Sounders.

item.title: Andoni Iraola handpicks Liverpool's next Mohamed Salah
item.description: Andoni Iraola handpicks Liverpool's next Mohamed Salah Mohamed Salah still hasn't been properly replaced at Liverpool. The attacker mutually agreed to terminate his contract at the end of last season and, even though the Reds didn't get any sort of transfer fee for him, they did manage to save around £20 million on his years worth of wages. If he'd have stayed, the Egyptian King would only have a year left on his deal anyway and, with the way that Andoni Iraola's system works , it's unclear how things would have turned out for him. Indeed, others such as Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz were added to Liverpool's ranks but, since they're both natural left-wingers rather than right-wingers, there's still a gap in the Reds' first-team squad that needs to be plugged. So, the fact that Iraola now seems to have chosen his very own version of Salah should be music to the ears of Liverpool fans. David Otorbi could become Liverpool's next Mohamed Salah Recently, news has broken which shared that Liverpool were willing to activate the €30 million release clause that was baked within David Otorbi's Valencia contract. The Spaniard has recently broken onto the La Liga scene and, although he has managed to contribute to many goals yet, his performances have caught the eye of Liverpool. Not only is he one of Valencia's fastest players but, he's also one of their best despite only being 19 years old. Several other clubs from around the world have been linked with an interest in him but, since he's a natural right-winger and is currently looking for his big break, it feels like he could become the Reds' next Salah. Indeed, he is right-footed so he won't be an exact carbon copy but, playstyle wise, Otorbi looks like the perfect successor. Liverpool must make their move for David Otorbi soon if they want to sign him Liverpool's interest in Otorbi has only just emerged. The Spaniard wasn't on the radar of any other clubs with Liverpool being one of the first teams linked with an actual interest in him. But, now that Valencia look likely to extend his deal and bump his release clause up to €60 million, the Reds are going to have to act fast if they want to sign him. Knowing the La Liga outfit, they'll try and hold out for the €60 million clause but, if they have another terrible season, as they did last term, they may not have that option to rely upon by the end of the term. At the moment, Liverpool's attack seems to be in a fairly solid place with some such as Cody Gakpo , Alexander Isak and even Bradley Barcola now getting back to their best . But, if Iraola and Julian Ward want to best prepare their attack for the future, Otorbi could be the best way for them to do that.

item.title: “Fun way to play football”: Elisabeth Terland reveals how happy Man United Women players are under Eva Olid
item.description: “Fun way to play football”: Elisabeth Terland reveals how happy Man United Women players are under Eva Olid Manchester United Women continue their improving performances with a solid 1-1 draw with champions Manchester City. Deserved draw The Red Devils played well but fell behind in the second half. Nonetheless, this did not deter them, and they forced an equaliser in the 89th minute through Elisabeth Terland. Her instinctive strike from inside the area was enough to secure a well-deserved draw for Eva Olid’s side. The Norwegian Sky Sports after the game. Terland comments The striker echoed her manager’s thoughts that the red side could have easily come away with the win. She explained, “I think, with the way the game evolved, we should be happy with a point. But I’m really happy with the performance today. To be honest, I think we could have gone away with a win. But yeah, we take a point at the end of the day.” Explaining what Eva Olid told them at half-time, she said, “just to go out and do the same, just one step better. I think we had the chances today to get even more goals, even in the first half. We should have been up. I think there’s a lot to take from this game, and this is the standard going forward.” Finally, the team have really turned a corner from the start of the season, and Terland was asked about this. She expressed her joy at being part of this group and feeling the progress. Terland explained, “it’s great. It’s a fun way to play football. I think if we can play like this every week, it’s something you enjoy so much.” Reflecting on the magnitude of the performance against Manchester City, she added, “I think we’re competing against a top team, and we should probably win the game. I think that just speaks for itself. But yeah, it’s a good performance.” United will next be in action at home to Burnley in the Players’ Cup on Wednesday evening. Featured image by Ben Roberts Photo via Getty Images

item.title: Seahawks Jaxon Smith-Njigba Delivers Simple Message After Beating Chiefs
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks carries the ball during the third quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba had a huge game against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs, then a simple message about the team’s next challenge. The reigning NFL receiving leader made nine catches for 150 yards and a touchdown, helping lead his team to a 20-3 victory over Kansas City. Speaking on the field after the game, Smith-Njigba had a simple, four-word statement about the win. Jaxon Smith-Njigba Moving on After Chiefs Win In a video the team shared on X, Smith-Njigba expressed gratitude that his team was able to grind out a win against the previously undefeated Chiefs. “What a great win,” he said. “What a great win. In front of the 12s, always great to be home.” Smith-Njigba then ended his statement with four words that put the win in perspective. “Onto the next, though,” he said. The win brought the Seahawks back over .500 at 4-3, helping them stay in the race for the NFC West. The San Francisco 49ers had suffered their first loss earlier in the day, falling to 6-1 after losing to the Atlanta Falcons. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Seahawks Jaxon Smith-Njigba Delivers Simple Message After Beating Chiefs appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings: Who leads race ahead of tonight’s ceremony
item.description: The race for the Ballon d’Or is all but over with the world’s best player set to be crowned in the glamorous London ceremony this evening. Harry Kane , Lamine Yamal and others have made their case, with a campaign from players, clubs and entourages filling pages and social media feeds for weeks. Spain’s triumph over Argentina in the World Cup final catapulted 2024 winner Rodri and Yamal into contention, though Barcelona pushed for the latter as their main contender, potentially avoiding a share of votes between the two international and club colleagues. Kane is the favourite , according to the bookmakers, and the Bayern Munich and England forward’s case is built behind a relentless run of production, both scoring and creating goals, to twist the narrative in his favour. During the World Cup, eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Lionel Messi showed that he can still force himself into the conversation at the age of 39, firing eight goals to propel Argentina to the final and briefly take the crown as the competition’s all-time top goalscorer - until he was eclipsed by Kylian Mbappe , while Sir David Beckham has tipped the Argentine to win after inspiring Inter Miami to the Campeones Cup. Here’s how the top 10 front-runners stack up in The Independent’s Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings: 10. Pau Cubarsi 🆕 What’s this, a new entry to the power rankings?! Barcelona’s Cubarsi is favourite to bring home the Golden Boy award, but he’s so far been bumped from our list by Vinicius Jr, who squeezed into our top 10 mainly to spare myself some angry emails from those affiliated to Real Madrid and Brazil (I joke, kind of). The 2024 runner-up had another strong season at the Bernabeu, netting 22 goals in 36 appearances, though was unable to inspire the club to a trophy. And after a below average start to the new term, with just one goal to his name in 10 as Real sit six points off the top, he’s been usurped by an El Clasico rival in Cubarsi. Despite still only being 19, Cubarsi is an established figure at the heart of the Barca and Spain defence, and after picking up the honour of Young Player of the Tournament following his country’s World Cup win, he has carried that impenetrable form back to the Camp Nou. The Blaugrana have won nine from nine in the league and haven’t looked close to suffering defeat. He’s up there among the best defenders on the planet as a teenager, playing a role that usually favours the more experienced; he will only get better. But does that mean Cubarsi will become the second player to ever win both the Golden Boy and Ballon d’Or on the same night after Messi? Doubtful. Pau Cubarsi was the Young Player of the Tournament at the World Cup (Getty) 9. Michael Olise ↔️ Crystal Palace could only keep him in Croydon for so long. With Bayern Munich and France, Olise has established himself as one of the world’s best attackers, a talent so bright that the German giants did well to ward off interest from the likes of Real Madrid - who no doubt saw the World Cup partnership he formed with Mbappe and want to reunite the pair in the Spanish capital at some stage. Will his electrifying performances be enough to win the Ballon d’Or? Probably not, this year. But he’s in the conversation, which is a statement in itself. The jury may also fear what an Olise acceptance speech might look like. If his post-match interview from Bayern’s opening Champions League win over Bodo/Glimt is anything to go by, in which he scored a brace and assisted another, it’ll be like getting blood out of a stone. The perils of the nonchalant gimmick. Michael Olise has proved himself as one of the world’s best attackers (Reuters) For unrivalled football insight from Miguel Delaney, join Inside Football here . 8. Erling Haaland ⬇️ On solely his performances, Haaland does not exactly deserve to drop down in these rankings as we hurtle towards the Ballon d’Or ceremony. So let’s start with the good. In the summer, Haaland was one of the stars of the World Cup and ensured Norway, playing in their first finals since 1998, lived up to their dark-horse status by powering them to the last-eight. On the way, his unrelenting goalscoring exploits humbled Brazil , sending the five-time winners packing. Away from the big-hitting nations, Haaland was far and away the tournament’s standout player, to little surprise. He has then followed up on a pretty bog-standard season for City - just the 38 goals last year, the fourth season he’s hit 30+ at the Etihad, and a domestic double - by starting the season with 12 goals in 10 appearances. The man can’t and won’t stop scoring. But, there’s a big but. Voting for the Ballon d’Or closed a few days after City’s guilty verdict was revealed. Currently, every bit of success related that club feels tainted. We feel that would have swayed some on the jury (not all) to vote against Haaland, whose goals are being financed by owners who inflated their own sponsorship income by £830m across eight seasons. He was already an outsider, but his odds have dropped further. Apologies Erling. Not your fault. Man City’s guilty verdict may have hurt Erling Haaland’s Ballon d’Or chances (Getty) 7. Jude Bellingham ⬆️ How was this man’s place on the England plane ever in question?! Thomas Tuchel’s player of the tournament, Bellingham served his critics a serious helping of humble pie by guiding the Three Lions to the elusive World Cup bronze. That beautiful redemption arc , on its own, got Bellingham onto this list. That’s because the season that preceded the World Cup wasn’t spectacular. Injuries limited him to just 13 goal contributions for Real Madrid in another trophyless campaign. However, he’s started the new season pretty well, and that keeps him on this list - seven goal contributions in nine league games shows he might be returning to his Madrid form of old under Jose Mourinho. He also just bagged four goal contributions in England’s 7-0 thumping of Croatia, the first midfielder to do so in a single match for the Three Lions since David Platt scored four against San Marino in February 1993. His chances of winning the Ballon d’Or are still low compared to the competition. But as was proved at the World Cup - maybe don’t count him out. Jude Bellingham has continued to be indispensable for England since the World Cup (Getty) 6. Ousmane Dembele ⬆️ Had France won the World Cup, as many expected them to do leading up to that drab semi-final exit , Dembele would have been heavily favoured to secure a second successive Ballon d’Or. The combination of World Cup and Champions League winners’ medals is a bit of a cheat code. That would’ve been quite the gimme for a player who, let’s be honest, was France’s fourth best attacker at the World Cup. And while, like last year, he ended the season as Paris Saint-Germain’s top scorer with a Ligue 1 and Champions League to boot, he only managed about half of his goalscoring output. His trophy haul still carries enough weight to be comfortably in the top 10 contenders, but the failure to lift that World Cup title gives him only an outside chance to go back-to-back - and we think that’s fair. His slow start to the new campaign, only scoring his first league goal last weekend, doesn’t help his cause. Sorry Ousmane, but this year shouldn’t be your year. Ousmane Dembele won back-to-back Champions Leagues with PSG (PA) 5. Lionel Messi ↔️ He couldn’t again, could he? Messi’s inclusion on this list encapsulates the significance of the World Cup in deciding the Ballon d’Or winner; he’s not going to take the accolade for his MLS exploits, is he. But fair play to the eight-time winner; at 39, he showed he very much still had it. Messi’s eight goals propelled Argentina to the World Cup final, where they were rightly defeated by Spain - had he lifted back-to-back titles, he’d probably be towards the top two of this list. After all, he claimed the 2023 award after La Albiceleste’s triumph 10 months earlier, by which time he was on t

item.title: Russell says second spot would mean nothing as Antonelli nears title
item.description: Mercedes' George Russell during the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of The Americas in Austin, Texas. (is associated with: «Russell says second spot would mean nothing as Antonelli nears title») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa George Russell says finishing second in the championship would not mean anything as boss Toto Wolff hit back at suggestions that the British driver may never get another shot at the title. The 28-year-old trudged home eighth at the United States Grand Prix on Sunday, the bare minimum he needed to keep the title race mathematically alive as leader Kimi Antonelli roared to a dominant victory. Antonelli now holds a whopping 123-point lead over his team-mate, with Lewis Hamilton still just about in it a point further back. Russell also now has Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc within 10 points of him. While the Italian is likely to be celebrating the championship in Mexico City next weekend, Russell is not driven by the fight to finish second. "As long as we win the constructors' championship, that's the main thing," a dejected Russell said. "Obviously I'd like to finish best of the rest but P2, P3, P5 is not champion, so it doesn't mean anything." Antonelli was in a league of his own in Austin, romping home a huge 13.0 seconds ahead of Leclerc. But Russell, hampered by an early five-second penalty, had no answer in the same machinery, unable to get past McLaren's Oscar Piastri to progress from eighth. "Six good laps, 50 bad laps," Russell added. "The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that's the least of my worries after such a bad weekend. "He obviously was exceptionally competitive and there are signs that the window (of performance) is very small. I hope that's an explanation for my lack of pace today, but I need to believe in my team because it's difficult to understand when you're so far off." Russell entered the season as heavy title favourite in the grid's dominant car but his young team-mate has turned the tables and is set to storm to the title. Former Red Bull motorsport advisor Helmut Marko told Sky Deutschland this week that he doubted Russell would ever get another shot at the championship, having been usurped as Mercedes' number one. Team principal Wolff hit back at that assertion, saying: "I think he's (Marko) wrong on George. George has all the ability. I think the car doesn't suit him. "I think that at the beginning of the season it's difficult to cope with a situation where you're feeling like 'this is my year to come', and then you have this wunderkind on the other side that starts to really chip away. "And I believe that in a new season, George, if we provide him a quick car, has absolutely what it needs to win a championship." Wolff also believes it is down to the team to understand Russell's deficit to Antonelli, taking blame away from his driver. "George, for all of us in the team, is a champion and has won in every category. I think he merits to be put in the group of the very best ones," Wo

Because it's all there - intelligence, ability, determination."

item.title: 'I don't think we can reveal on live TV': Shadab Khan on chat with Haris Rauf
item.description: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan had plenty to say about his conversation with Haris Rauf during their match-winning partnership against England. After guiding Pakistan to a thrilling one-wicket win in Lahore on Sunday, Shadab revealed that the two were talking more about things other than cricket. “He was explaining things to me more than I was explaining things to him. He was saying things along the way that I don't think we can reveal on live TV. I think we had a lot of fun moments and really enjoyed ourselves. We were talking more about other things than cricket,” Shadab said after being named Player of the Match. Their conversation seemed to work wonders as Pakistan pulled off a remarkable comeback. Chasing 242, the hosts were struggling at 154-9 before Shadab and Rauf joined hands to take the team home. Shadab, Rauf script record partnership Shadab remained unbeaten on 113, while Rauf scored seven not out off 19 balls. The pair added 89 runs for the last wicket, the highest partnership for the final wicket in a successful ODI run chase. Pakistan needed a strong finish after England's bowlers had put them on the back foot. Shadab struck 13 fours and five sixes to lead the fightback, while Rauf played a crucial supporting role. Shadab was given out lbw with Pakistan needing 21 runs to win. However, he reviewed the decision and survived after replays showed an inside edge. Reflecting on the partnership, Shadab said Rauf deserved more credit for helping Pakistan cross the finish line. “Obviously, you only enjoy an innings when the team wins. So, I'm very happy that I played that innings and we won the match. I think Haris deserves more credit than me because, obviously, tailenders at that position are always keen to hit sixes. The way I was guiding him, or he was guiding me, we managed to put together a good partnership.” Shadab reveals what kept him going at 154-9 Pakistan looked close to defeat when Shadab found himself with the last man at the crease. However, the all-rounder said he kept believing that he could finish the job. “Obviously, I think you just go with the flow. When I made my comeback in the last series, there was an innings against Australia where I kept going until the end, but I couldn't win the match. So the idea was to keep believing. The conditions were a little different today, with dew coming in. I also felt their bowling was under a bit of pressure, given how things had gone in the previous match. I thought that if we could put them under pressure, they might end up bowling in areas that suited my game.” Afridi's four wickets put England under pressure Earlier, England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs after Ben Duckett scored a composed 105. Shaheen Shah Afridi led Pakistan's bowling attack with four wickets for 46 runs. Afridi struck in the first over to dismiss Tom Banton and removed Joe Root in the third. Haris Rauf then sent Jordan Cox back as England slipped to 52-4. Duckett and Sam Curran rebuilt the innings

Haris Rauf then sent Jordan Cox back as England slipped to 52-4. Duckett and Sam Curran rebuilt the innings with a 93-run partnership for the fifth wicket. Curran scored 42 before becoming Afridi's third victim. Jamie Overton helped England cross 200, while Gus Atkinson remained unbeaten on 36. Pakistan's chase also got off to a poor start as Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam fell for 10 each. Saad Baig scored a quick 32 off 22 balls, while Salman Ali Agha made 26, but Pakistan continued to lose wickets. Shadab arrived at the crease in the 24th over with Pakistan at 103-6. His unbeaten century eventually turned the match around and secured a place for the hosts in the tri-series final. The defeat was England's third consecutive loss in the tri-series. They had earlier suffered a heavy blow when Sri Lanka chased down 430 with one ball remaining, completing the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.

item.title: F1 Mexican GP 2026: All session times and full weekend schedule
item.description: Formula 1 heads to Mexico City for the Mexican Grand Prix, where Kimi Antonelli could take the final step towards his maiden World Championship. The Mercedes driver arrives at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez with a genuine match point, following his first mathematical opportunity to seal the title at the United States Grand Prix in Austin. The Italian youngster is approaching a potentially historic moment in his Formula 1 career. Although the championship mathematics already gave him an opportunity in Texas, Mexico presents another chance to settle the fight for the crown before the season reaches its final rounds. The Mexican Grand Prix takes place from 30 October to 1 November, with the demanding Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez providing the backdrop for the weekend. Located at an altitude of more than 2,200 metres above sea level, the circuit presents unique challenges for teams, particularly in terms of cooling and aerodynamic performance. What time is the 2026 Mexican Grand Prix? As in Austin, Formula 1 will use its traditional weekend format in Mexico, with three practice sessions before Saturday's qualifying and Sunday's race. The opening session gets underway on Friday, 30 October, at 19:30 CET (18:30 UK time), followed by FP2 at 23:00 CET (22:00 UK time). Teams will use the two sessions to gather data and assess their setups on a circuit where the thin air can significantly affect car performance. Saturday's action begins with FP3 at 18:30 CET (17:30 UK time), providing one final opportunity to make adjustments before qualifying starts at 22:00 CET (21:00 UK time). George Russell and Kimi Antonelli during 2025 Mexican Grand Prix George Russell and Kimi Antonelli during 2025 Mexican Grand Prix The race itself is scheduled for Sunday, 1 November, at 21:00 CET (20:00 UK time), bringing the weekend to its conclusion after 71 laps around the 4.304-kilometre circuit. For Antonelli, the stakes extend far beyond another race victory. The Mercedes driver has the chance to turn an outstanding campaign into a championship-winning season, with Mexico City potentially becoming the scene of his greatest achievement yet. Full 2026 Mexican GP schedule: UK and CET times

item.title: T.J. Hockenson Gets Candid on Kyler Murray Connection After Vikings Win
item.description: (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings moved to 6-0 after defeating the Indianapolis Colts 16-10 in Week 7 on Oct. 25. Moreover, despite only scoring 16 points, the Vikings continue to see a growing connection between Kyler Murray and T.J. Hockenson. Hockenson was one of Murray’s go-to targets in the win as the veteran tight end recorded four receptions on five targets for 35 receiving yards and one touchdown. After the win over the Colts, Hockenson spoke with the media and shared his thoughts on the connection he has been having with Murray over the last couple of weeks. “I guess he trusts me where I feel space, I feel zones, I feel where the defense is and kind of where to sit and find the voids,” Hockenson told reporters postgame . “He sees that, and he sits back there and feels that too. As a quarterback, you want somebody you’re not going to keep running to get covered or keep doing this to make it a harder throw. “So I just try to make easy throws for him and find zones and see what we’re able to work. That’s something I pride myself in. I’ve always had to be able to be on the same page with the quarterback.” T.J. Hockenson on Kyler Murray’s 35-Yard Scramble Moreover, Hockenson shared what went through his mind during Murray’s 35-yard scramble as the Vikings QB showed that he can lean on his legs when needed and make a big play for the team. “That was a weird look,” Hockenson added. “They played man. That was a tough one for me. He had hard inside leverage on an inside-breaking route, so I was like, ‘All right, well,’ and then he just kept following me, and Kyler took off. He’s so fast. “There are so many times when you’re going to scramble, and then he’s on you, and you’re like, ‘Oh, I should have blocked,’ or ‘I should have gone deeper,’ or whatever. He’s so fast, so it’s still about getting in that rhythm with him. When he gets those legs moving, it’s hard to stop him, and it’s a good aspect to have as an offense.” Vikings Had Another Slow Start Offensively Meanwhile, while the Vikings did come away with the win and that’s all that matters at the end of the day, the Minnesota offense did get off to another slow start. The Vikings only recorded six first-half points, and while they can lean on their defense to help them out, it’s an issue that they need to figure out. After defeating the Colts, Murray spoke about another slow first-half start from the team. “I feel like we moved the ball well today, and nobody wants to hear that in that locker room offensively,” Murray said postgame . “We got to put the ball in the end zone. At the end of the day, that’s what it comes down to. But I did feel like we did some good things. “Got to go back and watch it, but we’ll continue to get better. I know we will, and I know everybody, we keep saying that, but like I said, I felt like we moved the ball well today. We just got to put the ball in the end zone.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post T.J. Hockens
