item.title: Pundit Claims Arsenal Will ‘100 Per Cent’ Sell Gyökeres Next Summer
item.description: Pundit Claims Arsenal Will ‘100 Per Cent’ Sell Gyökeres Next Summer Former Aston Villa striker Gabriel Agbonlahor has made a bold prediction about Viktor Gyökeres’ Arsenal future, insisting the Gunners will sell the Swedish international next summer. His comments followed Arsenal’s comfortable 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday, a match in which Gyökeres provided an assist but once again failed to get himself on the scoresheet. And Agbonlahor clearly wasn’t impressed with what he saw. Agbonlahor Questions Gyökeres’ Arsenal Future Speaking on talkSPORT , Agbonlahor questioned the striker’s mobility. “Looks like he’s like running in slow motion, isn’t he?” He then acknowledged that Gyökeres can hold the ball up, but insisted the 28-year-old would not be at Arsenal next season, confirming: “Yeah, 100%.” Agbonlahor went further, suggesting Arsenal would already have moved Gyökeres on if they had managed to secure the signing of Atlético Madrid forward Julián Álvarez. Of course, this isn’t a new idea. Arsenal were repeatedly linked with a Gyökeres-plus-cash deal for Álvarez throughout the summer transfer window, with one report suggesting the Gunners could offer the Swedish striker alongside £68.5 million. Ultimately, nothing materialised, and Gyökeres remained at Arsenal. But Agbonlahor clearly believes the club will revisit the question of his future next summer. That’s quite a statement about a player who helped Arsenal win the Premier League last season and remains under contract until 2030. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Is Gyökeres Really Finished at Arsenal? There is no denying that Gyökeres has struggled for goals this season. He managed just 17 touches and failed to register a shot during his 68 minutes against Everton. For a striker who arrived with such an impressive goalscoring reputation, those numbers are naturally disappointing. However, Gyökeres has contributed assists in consecutive appearances, helping Arsenal secure positive results even without scoring himself. And Saturday was only his first Premier League start of the campaign. It’s certainly fair to question whether Gyökeres is producing enough to justify a regular starting place, particularly with Kai Havertz competing for the same position. But suggesting Arsenal will definitely sell him next summer seems premature when we’re only eight league games into the season. Arteta has repeatedly spoken positively about the striker, and there is still plenty of football to be played before any decisions about next summer’s transfer window need to be made. Perhaps Agbonlahor will eventually be proved right. But surely Gyökeres deserves more than one league start before his Arsenal future is written off? Join the discussion in the comments below. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. You agree not to give any personal abuse to other Arsenal

Agbonlahor Questions Gyökeres’ Arsenal Future Speaking on talkSPORT , Agbonlahor questioned the striker’s mobility. “Looks like he’s like running in slow motion, isn’t he?” He then acknowledged that Gyökeres can hold the ball up, but insisted the 28-year-old would not be at Arsenal next season, confirming: “Yeah, 100%.” Agbonlahor went further, suggesting Arsenal would already have moved Gyökeres on if they had managed to secure the signing of Atlético Madrid forward Julián Álvarez. Of course, this isn’t a new idea. Arsenal were repeatedly linked with a Gyökeres-plus-cash deal for Álvarez throughout the summer transfer window, with one report suggesting the Gunners could offer the Swedish striker alongside £68.5 million. Ultimately, nothing materialised, and Gyökeres remained at Arsenal. But Agbonlahor clearly believes the club will revisit the question of his future next summer. That’s quite a statement about a player who helped Arsenal win the Premier League last season and remains under contract until 2030. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Is Gyökeres Really Finished at Arsenal? There is no denying that Gyökeres has struggled for goals this season. He managed just 17 touches and failed to register a shot during his 68 minutes against Everton. For a striker who arrived with such an impressive goalscoring reputation, those numbers are naturally disappointing. However, Gyökeres has contributed assists in consecutive appearances, helping Arsenal secure positive results even without scoring himself. And Saturday was only his first Premier League start of the campaign. It’s certainly fair to question whether Gyökeres is producing enough to justify a regular starting place, particularly with Kai Havertz competing for the same position. But suggesting Arsenal will definitely sell him next summer seems premature when we’re only eight league games into the season. Arteta has repeatedly spoken positively about the striker, and there is still plenty of football to be played before any decisions about next summer’s transfer window need to be made. Perhaps Agbonlahor will eventually be proved right. But surely Gyökeres deserves more than one league start before his Arsenal future is written off? item.title: ‘Have to’ – Klint Kubiak’s honest answer on Fernando Mendoza replacing Kirk Cousins as Raiders QB1
item.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza with the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but haven’t let him start a game yet. Rather than put that pressure on Mendoza, the Raiders signed and have started Kirk Cousins in every game this season. Cousins is a veteran who can help Mendoza develop his game in training, and has been trusted to keep the Raiders afloat this season. Klint Kubiak’s honest answer on Fernando Mendoza becoming Raiders QB1 Speaking after the Las Vegas Raiders’ 21-35 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked whether he will consider starting Fernando Mendoza as QB1. After what has been an inconsistent 3-4 start, Kubiak is ready to review the game footage and consider all his options, including starting Mendoza. Kubiak said: “I think we have to go watch the film. At this point, we’re thinking about everything – how to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter and personnel scheme. We have got to talk about all of it.” So far, Kirk Cousins has started every game for the Raiders, with Mendoza getting just a few minutes against the New England Patriots late in the Raiders’ Week 4 game. But with the Raiders now hoping to turn their fortunes around and make an unlikely push for the playoffs, they might have to start giving Mendoza more opportunities going forward. In their loss against the Rams, Cousins threw for 295 yards with two touchdowns. Unfortunately, he was also sacked twice, which allowed the Rams to gain control during the game. The Raiders see Mendoza as their long-term quarterback and don’t want to rush him into a high-pressure environment so early in his career. This is a strategy other teams have employed with star-level young quarterbacks. Most notably, the Chiefs used this approach with Patrick Mahomes during his rookie year. But with the Raiders where they are, Kubiak and the rest of the coaching staff will have to consider pulling the trigger on Mendoza early. item.title: Jose Mourinho talks Silva, Lunin, Camavinga, Cucurella after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid
item.description: Jose Mourinho talks Silva, Lunin, Camavinga, Cucurella after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid Last night was one to remember for Real Madrid fans as they saw their team visit the Spotify Camp Nou and get a 1-2 win over their arch-rivals FC Barcelona. As was expected, it turned out to be a hard-fought game in which both the teams tried their best to get a result in their favor, but ultimately, the Merengues’ quality shone through and they come back to the Spanish capital reducing the deficit at the top of the La Liga table to three points. As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed the press after this enthralling win. Analyzing the match, the Portuguese coach praised his team for giving their all on the pitch: “It’s been a great match, a high-level game. Two teams that play to win, and in our case, the lads put in a great performance. They were organised and courageous against an opponent who presses a lot. We had chances to score a second goal, including that two-against-one situation with Jude and Kylian. Barça reacted strongly in the second half, but we remained calm and didn’t lose our composure. It was a great victory for the lads. The referee had a great game. VAR was asleep in the 60th minute, with a decision that had a major impact on João’s clear red-card offence for the foul on Diomande.” The Real Madrid coach highlighted how important this win could be for the league title, and praised several players for their performances in this game: “It’s a match that could leave us three, six or nine points clear. If you come away nine points ahead, that’s a significant gap. If it’s six, things are more balanced. If it’s three, the situation is different. You can win through luck or by spending much of the game defending, but we won comfortably and fully deserved it. I’ve only been here a short time with Bernardo, although I know him well. item.content:encoded: Jose Mourinho talks Silva, Lunin, Camavinga, Cucurella after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid Last night was one to remember for Real Madrid fans as they saw their team visit the Spotify Camp Nou and get a 1-2 win over their arch-rivals FC Barcelona. As was expected, it turned out to be a hard-fought game in which both the teams tried their best to get a result in their favor, but ultimately, the Merengues’ quality shone through and they come back to the Spanish capital reducing the deficit at the top of the La Liga table to three points. As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed the press after this enthralling win. Analyzing the match, the Portuguese coach praised his team for giving their all on the pitch: “It’s been a great match, a high-level game. Two teams that play to win, and in our case, the lads put in a great performance. They were organised and courageous against an opponent who presses a lot. We had chances to score a second goal, including that two-against-one situation with Jude and Kylian. Barça reacted strongly in the second half, but we remained calm and didn’t lose our composure. It was a great victory for the lads. The referee had a great game. VAR was asleep in the 60th minute, with a decision that had a major impact on João’s clear red-card offence for the foul on Diomande.” The Real Madrid coach highlighted how important this win could be for the league title, and praised several players for their performances in this game: “It’s a match that could leave us three, six or nine points clear. If you come away nine points ahead, that’s a significant gap. If it’s six, things are more balanced. If it’s three, the situation is different. You can win through luck or by spending much of the game defending, but we won comfortably and fully deserved it. I’ve only been here a short time with Bernardo, although I know him well. That’s one thing; seeing how he can fit into the team is another. I’ll never tell you, ‘This is my core team’, or talk about indispensable players. We have a complete squad. They work hard and are ready to win. You’ve asked me two questions, and neither has been about Lunin. If Lunin makes mistakes, I’m sure the second question will be about him. We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but none of the players complained before the match because he wasn’t playing. The players are united. We’ve won five matches in a row, and we have another game on Sunday, in a unique run of three consecutive away matches. Valverde played injured for more than 40 minutes. He wanted to keep going within his limits.” While praising Eduardo Camavinga, Mourinho explained how his team got over the offside trap set by Flick’s team: “Eduardo, like everyone else, is a starting-calibre player. They train for that, and then it’s the manager who decides. Some managers look at the bench and have no solutions. Flick brought on De Jong, who is a very powerful engine. Bernardo worked hard against Pedri, and the match required us to bring on fresh legs to keep going and launch counter-attacks. Against Barcelona, it’s often difficult to attack the space because you frequently get caught offside. When the runs come from the second line, as Jude and Camavinga did, it’s harder for them to deal with.” Although his team won by the barest of margins, the Portuguese coach was happy with the result: “I think this was our toughest match against an opponent who had won every league game up to this point. We’ve beaten several teams by four goals, but this was Barça, and our players put in a great performance.” Mourinho highlighted how his team has improved over the last few weeks: “We’ve improved a lot in recent matches. I don’t want to go back to the Atlético game, but the Betis match was the one in which we missed the most chances. We didn’t play terribly. The group is strong internally, with a growing sense of empathy, and the players support one another. It’s a great group to work with. A great group is also one that sticks together when things get difficult. When we return to work, I won’t let everyone walk around with their heads in the clouds. If we lose at El Sardinero, today’s victory will mean nothing. Madrid play to win titles.” The Real Madrid coach also highlighted Marc Cucurella’s incredible performance in this match: “We have two high-level left-backs, which allows me to manage their workload a little. Carreras played the previous match, allowing Cucu to be fresh for this one. He did a great job. I always say that I only realise how good players are when I see them in front of me. Watching them on television, I miss certain things. When they’re ten metres away, I can appreciate their quality. He’s very good (Lamine), extremely difficult to handle and, as well as being talented, he’s clever. He tried everything. This was the toughest match Cucu has faced against a player who is really good.” The Portuguese coach was willing to give all the credit for this win to the players: “We won because of the players. That’s the life of a manager, and it’s why so many lose their jobs. I’m very happy for them, for all of them. I’m also happy for Asencio, who wanted to come today and has been talking to the players.” Finally, the Real Madrid coach highlighted his midfield option: “I’ve learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mentality to play. In midfield, too, having a combination of different talents gives us more than having two players with similar characteristics. That’s why I wouldn’t play Bernardo alongside Güler, except perhaps in desperate situations. The same goes for Camavinga and Tchouaméni today; that combination is for specific circumstances. This blend of talents gives us balance when defending and quality when building attacks.” Although he was gracious enough to give all the credit to his players, there is no doubt Jose Mourinho himself deserves a lot of credit for this memorable win. He clearly got the better of a coach as astute as Hansi Flick in this match, while his work in getting the best out of almost all the Real Madrid players and making the team work as a united group also deserve a lot of commendation.

item.title: ‘More Than a Bad Game,’ ‘This Is a Bad Sign’ — Ex-Eagles LB Sounds The Alarm as Chiefs’ Stalled Offense Hits Rock Bottom in Patrick Mahomes Era
item.description: 'More Than a Bad Game,' 'This Is a Bad Sign' — Ex-Eagles LB Sounds The Alarm as Chiefs' Stalled Offense Hits Rock Bottom in Patrick Mahomes Era The Kansas City Chiefs rolled into Lumen Field on Sunday night unbeaten and averaging an NFL-leading 414 yards a game. They left after scoring a mere three points in their first loss of the season, a 20-3 defeat to the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and a defeat that was a historic low in the Patrick Mahomes era. However, when former Eagles linebacker Emmanuel Acho broke down the game on his “Speakeasy” show postgame, he pointed to more worrying signs: “It’s more than just a bad game for the Chiefs. It’s a bad sign.” Emmanuel Acho Points to What Patrick Mahomes’ Chiefs Is Missing Kansas City went into Seattle short-handed at receiver and tackle. Tyquan Thornton, the team’s leading receiver, dislocated his ankle in the win over the Las Vegas Raiders and will miss at least three months after surgery. Rashee Rice has been out since hurting his hamstring in that game. Kansas City was also without starting tackle Jaylon Moore, while Josh Simmons had missed practice earlier in the week because of a back/personal matter. Acho began with the receivers: “Remember, his top two receivers are out, and one’s not coming back in Tyquan Thornton. So Patrick Mahomes is constantly asked to make high-quality lemonade out of limes. You feel me? How are you even going to do that? He’s asked to make high-quality lemonade out of limes, and at best, poverty lemons.” Mahomes’ longest completion on Sunday went for 19 yards. The Chiefs had piled up nearly 160 rushing yards a game through their first five outings, much of it from Kenneth Walker III, Seattle’s Super Bowl MVP last season. Walker came into Week 7 leading the league at 133 rushing yards a game, and ranking first in PFN’s NFL RB Impact Score with his 96.5 grade. Seattle, which hasn’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 games, held its former running back to a season-low 36 yards on 14 carries with no run longer than seven yards, and Kansas City finished with 50 rushing yards on 16 carries. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Acho then pointed to the Chiefs’ run game: “If you can stop the run game, hard to do, I get it. But if you can stop the run game, now Patrick Mahomes has to rely on Xavier Worthy, who hasn’t proven himself to be a bona fide number one, and an older Travis Kelce.” Kelce was held without a catch in the first half and finished with four grabs for 44 yards. That was enough to pass Marvin Harrison and Cris Carter for fifth on the NFL’s all-time receptions list. Acho closed with a warning: “There are a few teams that can do to the Chiefs what the Seahawks did to the Chiefs tonight, about three or so, and when you face those three or so teams, it will be bad.” How the Sunday Night Seahawks Loss Stacks Up in the Patrick Mahomes Era Several lows in the Chiefs’ Mahomes era stood out during their loss to the Seahawks on Sunday ni

However, when former Eagles linebacker Emmanuel Acho broke down the game on his “Speakeasy” show postgame, he pointed to more worrying signs: “It’s more than just a bad game for the Chiefs. He’s asked to make high-quality lemonade out of limes, and at best, poverty lemons.” Mahomes’ longest completion on Sunday went for 19 yards. The Chiefs had piled up nearly 160 rushing yards a game through their first five outings, much of it from Kenneth Walker III, Seattle’s Super Bowl MVP last season. Walker came into Week 7 leading the league at 133 rushing yards a game, and ranking first in PFN’s NFL RB Impact Score with his 96.5 grade. Seattle, which hasn’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 games, held its former running back to a season-low 36 yards on 14 carries with no run longer than seven yards, and Kansas City finished with 50 rushing yards on 16 carries. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Acho then pointed to the Chiefs’ run game: “If you can stop the run game, hard to do, I get it. But if you can stop the run game, now Patrick Mahomes has to rely on Xavier Worthy, who hasn’t proven himself to be a bona fide number one, and an older Travis Kelce.” Kelce was held without a catch in the first half and finished with four grabs for 44 yards. That was enough to pass Marvin Harrison and Cris Carter for fifth on the NFL’s all-time receptions list. Acho closed with a warning: “There are a few teams that can do to the Chiefs what the Seahawks did to the Chiefs tonight, about three or so, and when you face those three or so teams, it will be bad.” How the Sunday Night Seahawks Loss Stacks Up in the Patrick Mahomes Era Several lows in the Chiefs’ Mahomes era stood out during their loss to the Seahawks on Sunday night. The three points tied the fewest Kansas City has scored in a game Mahomes started, matching a 27-3 loss to the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 24, 2021. It was also only the third time in his career that the Chiefs failed to reach double figures. For the first time in a Mahomes start, Kansas City never reached the red zone. Its 213 yards were the lowest in a regular-season game he started, with only a 212-yard playoff win over the Houston Texans coming in lower. The Chiefs also went without an explosive play (a run of at least 10 yards or a pass of at least 20) for the first time in Andy Reid’s head-coaching career. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Mahomes finished 19 of 33 for 165 yards with no touchdowns, an interception, and a 58.3 passer rating, while Kansas City managed 11 first downs and converted 3 of 11 third downs. Harrison Butker supplied the only points with a 50-yard field goal. But he came up short from 58 as the first half expired, and in the fourth quarter he pushed a 45-yarder wide right that would have made it a one-possession game. Kansas City is still 5-1 and first in the AFC West, a half-game ahead of the 5-2 Denver Broncos. The Chiefs visit Denver on Sunday, Nov. 1, needing a win to stay top of the division. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Jets must end Aaron Glenn era after rock-bottom loss to previously winless Dolphins
item.description: Jets must end Aaron Glenn era after rock-bottom loss to previously winless Dolphins appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets have officially run out of excuses. Losing to a struggling divisional rival is frustrating enough. However, allowing the previously winless Miami Dolphins to leave MetLife Stadium with a 28-25 victory is nothing less than a damaging indictment of Aaron Glenn ’s leadership. New York entered Week 7 with a chance to stabilize its season and build on a narrow victory over Cleveland. Instead, the Jets struggled to contain Miami’s ground game and ultimately failed to complete a late comeback. At 2-5, New York’s central question is becoming impossible to avoid: Is Glenn still the right person to lead this franchise? Persistently problematic Brad Penner-Imagn Images New York’s 2026 campaign has been defined by missed opportunities and inconsistent execution. The Jets opened with a victory over Tennessee before dropping three straight games against Green Bay, Detroit, and Chicago. A 17-12 win over Cleveland briefly offered relief. However, a 26-19 defeat to New England sent them into their Week 7 matchup at 2-4. Sunday’s loss to Miami pushed them to 2-5, despite a spirited offensive response in the second half. Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Omar Cooper Jr. delivered 115 receiving yards. The Jets still fell short after allowing Miami to build a 21-7 halftime lead and produce 156 rushing yards. The Dolphins entered the game 0-5 and left with their first victory of the season. Defensive failure New York’s defense failed to impose its will against an offense that had struggled badly through the opening weeks. Miami quarterback Malik Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns. He repeatedly found ways to extend possessions. Running back Ollie Gordon II rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries. Miami converted all three of its fourth-down attempts, including a decisive quarterback sneak late in the fourth quarter that allowed it to drain the clock. New York could not consistently close running lanes or force Miami into the kind of mistakes that might have changed the game. The defense also failed to prevent a devastating 63-yard touchdown pass to Caleb Douglas late in the fourth quarter. That play restored Miami’s two-score cushion just when the Jets were threatening to take control. The late breakdowns were especially damaging because New York’s offense had done enough to make the game competitive. A head coach must find a way to get his team prepared for precisely these situations. Glenn’s defense repeatedly failed that test. A head coach must find a way to get his team prepared for precisely these situations. Glenn’s defense repeatedly failed that test. Not translating talent into wins New York’s roster has legitimate building blocks. Garrett Wilson remains a proven receiving threat . Breece Hall and Braelon Allen are dynamic running backs. The young receiving group has shown encouraging potential. Cooper’s performance against Miami was another positive sign. Tight end Mason Taylor caught two touchdown passes. Yet individual production has not translated into consistent winning football. The Jets have lost five of their first seven games. Their latest defeat came against a division opponent that had not won all season. Miami’s 14-point halftime lead came after the Jets struggled to respond to the Dolphins’ long possessions. New York had opportunities to limit the damage, but its defensive execution and late-half management left the team chasing the game. Stability is no longer enough Retaining Glenn simply because changing coaches is uncomfortable would be a questionable move forward. The franchise cannot afford to lose another season waiting for progress that has yet to materialize. The next few games should not become an indefinite extension of the same experiment. New York should evaluate the coaching staff’s performance honestly. They should start with its repeated struggles in high-leverage situations. If ownership believes Glenn cannot deliver meaningful improvement , making a change now would allow the organization to begin identifying the leadership it needs for 2027. Stop accepting old outcomes New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn looks on during the first half against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium. The Jets showed fight by scoring 18 points after halftime and pulling within three. Still, the comeback could not erase the failures that put them in that position. Miami converted a crucial fourth down, preserved possession, and secured its first win of the season. Glenn deserves a fair assessment, but his record demands serious scrutiny. New York needs accountability, sharper preparation, and a coaching structure capable of turning its talent into victories. At 2-5, the Jets still have a ton of games left to play. That said, the organization cannot keep pretending that patience alone will solve its problems. If Glenn cannot demonstrate that he can correct the defensive breakdowns and improve the team’s situational execution, New York should end the experiment. The loss to Miami may be remembered as the moment the Jets finally recognized that another change was necessary. item.title: Titans’ Robert Saleh refuses to admit he has a Cam Ward problem despite calling out bad misses
item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Titans’ Robert Saleh refuses to admit he has a Cam Ward problem despite calling out bad misses appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Cam Ward and Robert Saleh had a serious talk after the Tennessee Titans lost to the Houston Texans in Week 5, which kept them winless. It worked, as the Titans beat the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6 to end their losing skid. Well, it looks like Ward and Saleh might need to have another chat. The Titans bowed to the Cleveland Browns , 27-24, on Sunday, falling to 0-4 at Nissan Stadium. Ward went 20-of-31 for 181 yards, zero touchdowns, and one interception. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the second-year quarterback was subpar, Saleh stressed that their shortcomings against the Browns were “across the board,” as reported by ESPN’s Turron Davenport. “ Robert Saleh said there’s blame to go around on offense. Saleh admitted Cam Ward should have made some throws he missed, but he doesn’t think the offense has a quarterback problem,” wrote Davenport. Robert Saleh said there's blame to go around on offense. Saleh admitted Cam Ward should have made some throws he missed but he doesn't think the offense has a QB problem. pic.twitter.com/6ioWwBFSxT — TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) October 25, 2026 The 24-year-old Ward, last year’s No. 1 pick, could be in danger of losing his starting job in the coming weeks or being replaced next year if he fails to turn things around. Saleh has been patient with the young signal-caller, but at some point, he might have to acknowledge that the Titans could be better off with a different leader. The Titans struggled to limit the Browns’ running attack, with Quinshon Judkins getting 17 carries for 96 yards and two touchdowns. Deshaun Watson, who threw 25-of-36 for 308 yards, scored on a nine-yard rush in the fourth quarter. The defeat spoiled Tony Pollard’s outstanding effort. He logged 25 carries for 129 yards and a career-high-tying three touchdowns. Tennessee fell to 1-6, while Cleveland improved to 5-2. item.title: Andy Reid Breaks Silence on Josh Simmons’ Dismissal
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 22: Josh Simmons #71 of the Kansas City Chiefs watches the game from the sidelines during the second quarter during the NFL Preseason 2025 game between Chicago Bears and Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 22, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs took a disappointing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks Sunday night. After the game, coach Andy Reid faced some tough questions regarding his team’s performance. He also had to answer for the recent report of him dismissing offensive tackle Josh Simmons from a team meeting this past week. Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid Says Josh Simmons Being Placed on IR Had Nothing to Do With Meeting Dismissal Andy Reid said the Josh Simmons incident is not the reason he was put on IR. “He’s got a bad back.” — Sam McDowell (@SamMcDowell11) October 26, 2026 NFL insider Ian Rapoport recently reported that Reid, as well as quarterback Patrick Mahomes, made Simmons leave during a team meeting last Wednesday. Simmons reportedly had his feet up during the meeting, and gave push back when asked to put them down. Rapoport also revealed that Simmons later apologized for the situation. The Chiefs placed Simmons on injured reserve later that day. Following the team’s loss to the Seahawks, Reid insisted that Simmons being placed on IR had nothing to do with the incident. “Things happen,” Reid said. “That’s not the reason he was placed on IR. He’s got a bad back. He’s got to get it worked out, that’s the main thing. I’ll just leave it at that, that’s just where we’re at with it.” Josh Simmons’ Injury Timeline Simmons injured his back during training camp in early August. It was originally believed to be minor, and that he would be ready to play in Week 1 of the regular season. Many were surprised when he wasn’t able to, but the expectation was that he would only miss a couple of games. Because of that, the Chiefs avoided putting Simmons on IR. Reid eventually revealed that it was a bulging disc that was specifically ailing Simmons. He would go on to miss the first four games ahead of their Week 5 bye week. Simmons finally returned to practice after they bye, participating in all three sessions on a limited basis. He was held out of the Chiefs’ Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , as Reid stated he would need some time to ramp up. After Simmons missed this past Wednesday’s practice, the team trotted head athletic training Rick Burkholder out to address the media on Thursday regarding the injury. Burkholder revealed that Simmons was being placed on IR to give him more time to rehab and recover. Surgery isn’t completely off the table, but is trying to be avoided. Simmons will be eligible to return in Week 11 against the Arizona Cardinals . This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Andy Reid Breaks Silence on Josh Simmons’ Dismissal appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Mourinho hails 'extraordinary' Real Madrid after Mbappé double sinks Barcelona in El Clásico
item.description: Mourinho hails 'extraordinary' Real Madrid after Mbappé double sinks Barcelona in El Clásico José Mourinho says his Real Madrid players produced an 'extraordinary' performance after Kylian Mbappé's double secured a 2-1 Clásico win over Barcelona at Camp Nou. Mbappé opened the scoring in the 41st minute when Gerard Martín fired a clearance straight into him, before Raphinha levelled in the 61st minute. Mbappé then struck the winner in the 87th minute, tucking in Eduardo Camavinga's cutback after sublime skill from Jude Bellingham. The result ended Barcelona's perfect start to the season. Hansi Flick's side had won all nine of their La Liga fixtures and would have broken Madrid's 1968-69 record for the best ever start in the Spanish top flight with another win. Jose Mourinho's side had started the game six points behind their fierce rivals and knew defeat would have left them with a long road back in the title race. Mbappe's double instead sees Madrid move to 24 points from 10 games, three behind La Liga leaders Barcelona and one behind second-placed Atlético Madrid. The Frenchman's brace also continued a remarkable record in Spain's biggest fixture. Mbappe has now scored eight goals in seven Clásicos, and 14 goals in 11 career games against Barcelona. He also moved to 100 goals in 116 games for Real Madrid. Mourinho had insisted before the game that the Clásico would not decide whether his side can win things this season. "A game that the world which loves football stopped to see" Speaking after the match, Mourinho praised both sides for the spectacle before turning to his own players. "I think it was a great game," Mourinho said. "A game at a high level, a game that the world which loves football stopped to see. And they weren't let down, with two teams that played to win. "In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organised, focused, with a lot of courage, playing an opponent that presses you a lot. For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent. “This match was one where we could leave trailing by three, six, or nine points. Obviously, if you fall behind by nine, psychologically, it’s heavy. If we were behind by six, it would be balanced. Being three points behind is different, and the way we won is also important because you can win with luck and by defending a lot. We won calmly and with full merit.”

item.title: Celtic Confirm More Bad News After Hibernian Game
item.description: Many Celtic fans would have been viewing the game against Hibernian as a chance to get things back on track for the Hoops after their defeat at the hands of Celta Vigo in midweek. And although Martin O'Neill's side did win at Easter Road, it was not the confidence booster they would have been looking for. An own goal from Hibernian and a strike from Camilo Duran secured a 2-1 win for Celtic at the weekend against a team sitting at the bottom of the Scottish Premiership table. While O'Neill seemed content with the result coming out of the game, even happy, the same cannot be said about a lot of supporters. And it is not just the result they need to be worried about. The club have been handed fresh injury concerns as well. Celtic handed more bad news after Hibernian game Alistair Johnston is someone who has faced constant injury problems over his time at Celtic. Unfortunately, things don't seem to be getting any better for the Canadian international. Johnston was only making a return from injury in the game against Hibernian, coming on as a substitute. But he lasted only 20 minutes on the pitch before he had to be taken off again. As reported by beIN Sports , O'Neill said regarding Johnston's injury coming out of the game: "Alistair's felt something again, a little bit high up in his hamstring. A bit concerned about it. We don't know. We'll have to see. "That would be a blow if he's out. You never know. It might be cramp. It might be a number of things. "But he was really settling in brilliantly in the space of time that he was on the field." Obviously, that is far from ideal. Was he rushed back from injury? Or is this a player who simply can't stay fit anymore? Scottish FA Make Hibernian vs Celtic Match Announcement The Scottish FA have made an official announcement regarding the upcoming game between Hibernian and Celtic. Celtic need to start looking at life beyond Alistair Johnston On top of his game, Johnston is one of Celtic's best players. But due to his injury history, he is no longer someone the club can rely on. If Celtic are convinced that Colby Donovan is their long-term starter then they probably should start settling him into that role moving forward. If not, they should look to bring in someone who can take up that spot. As for Johnston, his time as a regular starter for Celtic might be as good as over. You simply cannot rely on a player who often spends more than half the season out injured. That is the unfortunate reality of the Canadian international's track record in recent times. The best-case scenario for Celtic would be for Johnston to somehow recover his fitness to a level where he can play consistent football. But the signs do not point in that direction, unfortunately.

item.title: ‘Cris Collinsworth Is So Unbelievably Cringeworthy,’ ‘Crazy’ — NFL Fans Rip NBC Broadcaster for ‘Glazing’ Patrick Mahomes After a Fumble
item.description: ‘Cris Collinsworth Is So Unbelievably Cringeworthy,’ ‘Crazy’ — NFL Fans Rip NBC Broadcaster for ‘Glazing’ Patrick Mahomes After a Fumble NBC analyst Cris Collinsworth showering Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes with over-the-top praise is nothing new. At this point, it has practically become a tradition during NFL broadcasts. Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks was no different. The Chiefs struggled to get anything going offensively and fell 20-3 to the reigning Super Bowl champions, but Collinsworth still found a moment to gush over Mahomes. It didn’t take long for fans to notice, and the clip quickly made the rounds on social media. Cris Collinsworth Takes Heat for His Boundless Praise of Patrick Mahomes The moment came in the third quarter, when Mahomes scrambled, took a hit, and fumbled the ball. The Chiefs quarterback then dove back into the pile and managed to recover it himself. Watching the replay, Collinsworth couldn’t help himself, saying, “What other quarterback is getting up twice to go get this football?” Collinsworth wasn’t done defending Mahomes, either. As the Chiefs’ offensive struggles continued, the NBC analyst turned his attention to the quarterback’s body language. “That’s the second time I’ve seen that look on Patrick Mahomes’ face. When he went back and recovered that fumble earlier, I saw that same sort of ‘I can’t believe this is happening to me’ look. There it is again. Have you ever seen that look on Patrick Mahomes?” he asked. Reacting to these moments, one fan tweeted , “Cris Collinsworth is so unbelievably cringeworthy when it comes to talking about Patrick Mahomes.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Associated Press reporter Rob Maaddi took issue with Collinsworth’s original point, arguing that recovering a fumble shouldn’t be treated as something extraordinary for a quarterback. “The question should be: Which QB doesn’t get up to go after a loose ball because that’s what would actually be rare,” he wrote . “Cris Collinsworth glazing Mahomes even after fumbling is crazy,” a third fan wrote on X. “Cris Collinsworth waxing poetic for Patrick Mahomes recovering his own fumble,” another fan commented . SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer One user struggled to wrap his head around the question, saying , “Patrick Mahomes got rocked and fumbled, and Cris Collinsworth somehow turns it into praising Mahomes.” After the loss, the Chiefs are 5-1 on the season and currently rank No. 6 in the league with a PFN Team Impact Score of 80.7. Kansas City’s Week 7 loss came down to several factors. The offense managed just 213 total yards, its lowest output in a regular-season game started by Mahomes. The Chiefs also failed to convert their first five third-down attempts and finished just 3-of-11 on third down. Mahomes’ struggles as a runner and his accuracy issues added to the offensive problems. Kansas City will look to bounce back against the Denver Broncos in Week 8. T

item.title: Chiefs’ Andy Reid delivers reality check for Harrison Butker after kicker’s SNF misses
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Chiefs’ Andy Reid delivers reality check for Harrison Butker after kicker’s SNF misses appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs had a Sunday night to forget, dropping a 20-3 loss against the Seattle Seahawks in a primetime matchup where virtually nothing went right. While the offense sputtered across four quarters, veteran kicker Harrison Butker endured an uncharacteristically rough outing that left head coach Andy Reid offering a firm reality check after the game. Butker converted just 1-of-3 field goal attempts on the night, finishing with a meager 33.3% success rate. The three-time Super Bowl champion did manage to drill a 50-yard field goal to put Kansas City on the scoreboard, but his two misfires proved exceptionally costly. The most agonizing pull came early in the fourth quarter on a 45-yard attempt. Trailing 13-3 at the time, a successful kick would have trimmed the deficit down to a single possession. Instead, the ball sailed wide right, deflating Kansas City’s sideline before Seattle pulled away late for the comfortable home victory. Addressing reporters during his postgame press conference, Reid delivered a candid assessment regarding his usually automatic placekicker’s recent form. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He’s been one of the most consistent kickers in football, but he’s off a bit — gotta fix it,” Reid said. Andy Reid on Harrison Butker's early-season struggles: “He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football, but he's off a bit — gotta fix it.” pic.twitter.com/MyPCz6j2JA — KC Sports Network (@KCSportsNetwork) October 26, 2026 Reid’s honest comments highlight growing concern over Butker’s early-season struggles. The Georgia Tech product earned a lucrative contract extension during the offseason that made him one of the highest-paid kickers in the National Football League. For years, Butker has served as Kansas City’s ultimate security blanket , routinely delivering clutch postseason heroics and long-range field goals with effortless precision. Seeing him misfire on manageable attempts raises immediate red flags for an elite contender that relies heavily on fine margins. The Chiefs simply cannot afford to leave free points on the turf as the regular season grind intensifies. Reid still holds full faith in his veteran specialist, but the takeaway remains crystal clear: Butker must recalibrate quickly before those missed kicks start turning tight contests into agonizing losses. Related: Did Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker III dodge ex-Seahawks teammates after SNF loss Related: Chiefs’ Travis Kelce reaches huge career milestone on National Tight Ends Day

item.title: Hansi Flick identifies Barcelona’s biggest problem after Real Madrid defeat: ‘We weren’t fresh’
item.description: Hansi Flick identifies Barcelona’s biggest problem after Real Madrid defeat: ‘We weren’t fresh’ Hansi Flick has admitted Barcelona were not physically fresh enough after suffering a 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season. The Barcelona manager refused to make excuses after his side lost at home, but acknowledged that fatigue, defensive injuries and a demanding schedule have affected the team’s performances. The defeat was Barcelona’s first in 10 La Liga matches and their second loss in the same week. Flick has now challenged his players to recover quickly, improve their energy levels and respond before the international break, while also considering further opportunities for La Masia prospects amid growing defensive concerns. Flick admits Barcelona lacked freshness against Real Madrid Flick was disappointed with Barcelona’s performance and acknowledged that Real Madrid had improved compared with previous meetings between the rivals. “We played against an opponent that was better than in previous Clásicos. We weren’t fresh. We have to recover, concentrate, and react. Flick admits Barcelona were not fresh. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “It’s not easy, but we have to accept it. Barça has to keep going.” The German manager also explained that Barcelona need to recover the physical sharpness they displayed earlier in the campaign. “Well, we have to try to switch off and forget about training. We need to regain the freshness we had in the previous matches of the season.” Flick felt Barcelona had performed better after the interval and had managed to restore parity, but their attacking commitment ultimately left them exposed to Madrid’s decisive counter-attack. “I’m not satisfied. Today it was clear we weren’t 100% fresh. Normally we would have been fresher. We played well in the second half, and Madrid only had two chances to score a second goal. “We controlled the game and scored to make it 1-1. In the end, we pressed high, and they countered and scored. “It’s not good for us, but we have to accept it. Defeats are also part of football,” Flick said. item.content:encoded: Hansi Flick identifies Barcelona’s biggest problem after Real Madrid defeat: ‘We weren’t fresh’ Hansi Flick has admitted Barcelona were not physically fresh enough after suffering a 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season. The Barcelona manager refused to make excuses after his side lost at home, but acknowledged that fatigue, defensive injuries and a demanding schedule have affected the team’s performances. The defeat was Barcelona’s first in 10 La Liga matches and their second loss in the same week. Flick has now challenged his players to recover quickly, improve their energy levels and respond before the international break, while also considering further opportunities for La Masia prospects amid growing defensive concerns. Flick admits Barcelona lacked freshness against Real Madrid Flick was disappointed with Barcelona’s performance and acknowledged that Real Madrid had improved compared with previous meetings between the rivals. “We played against an opponent that was better than in previous Clásicos. We weren’t fresh. We have to recover, concentrate, and react. Flick admits Barcelona were not fresh. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “It’s not easy, but we have to accept it. Barça has to keep going.” The German manager also explained that Barcelona need to recover the physical sharpness they displayed earlier in the campaign. “Well, we have to try to switch off and forget about training. We need to regain the freshness we had in the previous matches of the season.” Flick felt Barcelona had performed better after the interval and had managed to restore parity, but their attacking commitment ultimately left them exposed to Madrid’s decisive counter-attack. “I’m not satisfied. Today it was clear we weren’t 100% fresh. Normally we would have been fresher. We played well in the second half, and Madrid only had two chances to score a second goal. “We controlled the game and scored to make it 1-1. In the end, we pressed high, and they countered and scored. “It’s not good for us, but we have to accept it. Defeats are also part of football,” Flick said. The result has increased the pressure on Barcelona to respond, although Flick insisted that one defeat should not define the team’s campaign. “It’s our first defeat in ten league matches. We’re not playing at our best, and it’s related to freshness. “We have a week to prepare for the next match. We need to get the team’s energy back.” Flick refuses to make excuses after two defeats Barcelona’s recent results have raised questions about their ability to deliver in major matches. Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the La Liga season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Flick acknowledged the concerns and said the team needed to discuss what had gone wrong rather than look for explanations outside its control. “There are no arguments, no excuses – it’s clear. We need to talk. I’m not worried about it in general because, as I said before, it’s part of the sport. “We’ve had two defeats this week and that’s too many for me, and, no doubt, for the Barça fans as well. But this is part of the sport and we have to bounce back.” The manager also addressed the demanding travel schedule after Barcelona’s trip to Seville, although he was reluctant to use it to explain the Clasico loss. Several players are due to attend the Ballon d’Or Gala in London before returning to training. “In Seville, we spent three hours on the plane, then we stayed there to sleep. But I don’t want to talk about that now if we’ve lost. “Perhaps I’ll do so when we win, because it might sound like an excuse. Now many players will be going to London for the Ballon d’Or Gala, and they’ll be back. We’ll rest on Tuesday and get back to work on Wednesday. “I want to win both matches before the international break – it’s important. “Players like Espart, Olmo and Eric have picked up knocks and are injured. We don’t have many more options in defence and we’ll have to manage it.” Flick considers La Masia options amid defensive injury concerns Barcelona’s injury problems could force Flick to look towards the club’s academy as he attempts to manage the squad through the coming fixtures. Flick admits Barcelona might have to call up players from the youth team. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) With defensive options limited, the manager is hoping some injured players will return soon enough to ease the pressure. “We may have to call up more players from La Masia. We’ll sort it out. We’re expecting Christensen and Eric back soon. And we’ll see if we have any good news.” Flick also explained why Frenkie de Jong was introduced during the match, pointing to the midfielder’s recent training performances and the boost he could provide to the team. “We’ve been thinking about where to position him on the pitch. He’d been training well, he was giving us a boost, so we decided to bring him on and give him some playing time,” he concluded. Source: AS

item.title: Premier League Team of the Week: Our Best XI
item.description: Premier League Team of the Week: Our Best XI The Premier League Team of the Week is headlined by Aston Villa ’s statement victory over Manchester City, Tottenham’s impressive triumph at Chelsea and Bournemouth ’s latest demolition of Manchester United at Old Trafford. From Zion Suzuki’s outstanding display in goal to Nicolas Jackson ’s match-winning double, this week’s selection celebrates the players who made the biggest impact across the Premier League , with several summer signings continuing to make their mark. Goalkeeper: Zion Suzuki - Aston Villa It's time to give Aston Villa their flowers for their summer rebuild. There were fears when several senior stars were sold in the summer, but Villa look to have recruited brilliantly. Zion Suzuki has made his presence felt in goal and recorded 1.74 Expected Goals prevented against Manchester City. Right-back: Matty Cash - Aston Villa Summed up an excellent performance from Aston Villa with a dogged defensive display against Manchester City. Jeremy Doku is one of the most difficult direct opponents in the Premier League , but Cash gave everything in their one-vs-one battle. Eight tackles emphasised his good work. Centre-back: James Hill - Bournemouth James Hill might be one of the most under-appreciated players in the Premier League. Since breaking in as a Bournemouth regular last season, Hill has been immense. At Manchester United he was superb again, leading the contest for tackles and clearances. A big win for Bournemouth, who have made Old Trafford a playground in recent years. Centre-back: Gabriel - Arsenal Arsenal 's aerial threat returned against Everton with centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel on the scoresheet in a 2-0 win at the Emirates. Gabriel's emphatic header made the result safe, after a performance that saw the big Brazilian dominate his duel with Thierno Barry. The left-back punished Leny Yoro's slip to set up Marcus Tavernier's goal, continuing on the form that saw him earn an international call up for France under Zinedine Zidane. Central midfield: Nico Gonzalez - Newcastle Looked a class above as Newcastle earned an important three points at Crystal Palace. The Spaniard snapped into tackles, picking up a booking in the process, but dealt with that setback with trademark cool. Came out on top in his duel with Adam Wharton. item.title: Mourinho talks Cucurella, Diomande, Camavinga, Bernardo, Lunin after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid
item.description: Mourinho talks Cucurella, Diomande, Camavinga, Bernardo, Lunin after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid Jose Mourinho had plenty to celebrate after Real Madrid secured a 2-1 victory over Barcelona in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season, but the Portuguese manager also found time to deliver a cheeky message to the home supporters. Speaking after the match, Mourinho joked that Barcelona fans had prevented him from taking his usual afternoon nap before the game, before explaining how his tactical decisions, squad depth and Eduardo Camavinga’s decisive contribution helped Madrid secure the win. The Real Madrid manager also praised Marc Cucurella for his performance against Lamine Yamal, highlighted Yan Diomande’s defensive contribution and backed Andriy Lunin after the goalkeeper stepped in for Thibaut Courtois. Mourinho takes a playful dig at Barcelona fans Mourinho opened his post-match comments by dedicating the victory to the Barcelona supporters whose singing outside the team hotel had disrupted his rest before the game. “I dedicate this win to the Barca fans that did not let me take my nap in the hotel today. “They came to the hotel and they kept singing all day, so I couldn’t take my nap. Well, I didn’t nap, but I did beat their team. A big hug to them.” The remark captured Mourinho’s ability to add personality to a major victory. More importantly for Real Madrid, the result gave his team a significant psychological boost in a fixture that can have consequences well beyond the three points on offer. Mourinho also praised Cucurella’s discipline against Yamal and credited Diomande for limiting Barcelona’s options on the opposite flank. Mourinho had nothing but praise for Cucurella. item.content:encoded: Mourinho talks Cucurella, Diomande, Camavinga, Bernardo, Lunin after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid Jose Mourinho had plenty to celebrate after Real Madrid secured a 2-1 victory over Barcelona in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season, but the Portuguese manager also found time to deliver a cheeky message to the home supporters. Speaking after the match, Mourinho joked that Barcelona fans had prevented him from taking his usual afternoon nap before the game, before explaining how his tactical decisions, squad depth and Eduardo Camavinga’s decisive contribution helped Madrid secure the win. The Real Madrid manager also praised Marc Cucurella for his performance against Lamine Yamal, highlighted Yan Diomande’s defensive contribution and backed Andriy Lunin after the goalkeeper stepped in for Thibaut Courtois. Mourinho takes a playful dig at Barcelona fans Mourinho opened his post-match comments by dedicating the victory to the Barcelona supporters whose singing outside the team hotel had disrupted his rest before the game. “I dedicate this win to the Barca fans that did not let me take my nap in the hotel today. “They came to the hotel and they kept singing all day, so I couldn’t take my nap. Well, I didn’t nap, but I did beat their team. A big hug to them.” The remark captured Mourinho’s ability to add personality to a major victory. More importantly for Real Madrid, the result gave his team a significant psychological boost in a fixture that can have consequences well beyond the three points on offer. Mourinho also praised Cucurella’s discipline against Yamal and credited Diomande for limiting Barcelona’s options on the opposite flank. Mourinho had nothing but praise for Cucurella. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “We’ve got two top-class left-backs, which means I can rotate them a bit. Carreras played on Wednesday, and that allowed Cucu to be fresh, focused and thinking only about this match. “Obviously he was up against a great player, but he’s his teammate and knows him well. “I always say that I only really understand how good players are when I see them right in front of me – when I’m on the touchline. “He is very good, but he’s also clever. He tried everything to get Cucu booked, but Cucu held his ground well, and Diomande very rarely let Espart or Cancelo get the better of him. “A great team effort. But Cucu… he was excellent against a very good opponent.” Mourinho explains midfield balance and Camavinga decision Real Madrid’s tactical adjustments were another major talking point. Mourinho explained that the team’s recent performances had reinforced his belief in combining midfielders with different strengths rather than relying on players with similar characteristics. “That I have an extraordinary squad, with every player possessing the quality and mentality to play. “I’ve learnt that in midfield… having a mix of talents gives us more than having two players with similar characteristics. “And by that I mean that the Bernardo-Güler double pivot… I don’t use it. Or only in desperate situations. “But the double pivot we finished with today – Camavinga and Tchouameni – will also only be used at specific moments. I’m enjoying it. “I think the people at the top like this mix too, because it gives us balance in defence and more quality when it comes to building from the back.” Camavinga played a crucial role in Real Madrid’s match-winning goal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Mourinho then detailed why Camavinga’s introduction proved important, particularly after Barcelona brought Frenkie de Jong onto the pitch. The Madrid manager wanted fresh legs to sustain the press and exploit openings during transitions, with Camavinga instructed to attack spaces from deeper positions. “Camavinga, like everyone else, is a first-team player. There are times when you want to make substitutions; you look at the bench, and many managers suffer because they have no options, because they’re unable to implement their ideas. But I’ve got a strong bench. “Camavinga had an extraordinary match against Leipzig; today he was on the bench. Flick brought on De Jong, who’s a real powerhouse, to face Bernardo, who’d been working hard against Pedri for a long time… “The match needed fresh legs to keep up the pressing and to launch counter-attacks. “And I told Camavinga that, obviously, it was Tchouameni who was covering that position due to his attributes and having picked up a yellow card… and that he had to attack the spaces – something that’s difficult against Barcelona, because often you attack and you’re offside or the goalkeeper is off his line. “If the run comes from the second line, as Camavinga did, it’s more difficult for them. Things went well. A great match; the team deserved more.” Mourinho backs Lunin and refuses to declare a first choice team Asked whether the victory could prove a turning point in the season, Mourinho emphasised both the psychological importance of the result and the manner in which Real Madrid earned it. Andriy Lunin put on a great performance vs Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “This was a match where we could have come away with three, six or nine points. Obviously, if you come away with nine, it’s a psychological burden. “The way we won is also different. Because you can win with a bit of luck, but we did it calmly and fully deserved it.” The manager also insisted that his starting lineup would remain flexible, pointing to the quality and competitiveness within the squad. He used the discussion around Bernardo’s selection to explain why he would not commit to a fixed first-choice team. “On the selection of Bernardo… I’ve only been here a little over three months. And although I know him well, that’s one thing; knowing how he can slot into the team’s dynamics is quite another. “The squad is very strong. I’ll never say that this is my first-choice team or that this line-up is set in stone, because the squad is very good and well-rounded. The lads work hard. Everyone is ready. “And that’s just how it is. You’ve already asked me two questions and neither was about Lunin, but if we lose here because of mistakes he makes, the first or second question would be about him. “I’ve only said to him, ‘You train to play, not to sit on the bench; go and play.’ And he’s put in a performance with great composure and poise. “We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but today none of us has been upset that Thibaut isn’t playing,” he concluded. Source: AS

item.title: Crystal Palace 0 Newcastle 2 match ratings and comments on all Newcastle United players
item.description: Dan Burn Newcastle United celebrating win at Crystal Palace We asked Davey Hat-Trick to give us his match ratings and player comments after Crystal Palace 0 Newcastle 2 in the Premier League. A much-needed win, deserved if not emphatic. The first half looked like a turgid relegation scrap between two poor teams and I understand that. The weather was foul, neither team had any reason to feel optimistic given recent PL results, and a defeat would have put either team on the ‘clubs-in-crisis’ list. Our manager didn’t do what a lot of fans were hoping and play the majority of the young lads. Instead, he opted for a centre back pairing with a combined age of 68, and a very recognisable midfield and front four. I wouldn’t have gone with a few of those selected but it turned out to be exactly the right call. Newcastle United took control in the second half and won a game that a different XI may well have lost. The performance wasn’t spectacular and it’s only fair to highlight the shortcomings evident in our opponents. But forget what kind of display this was. What it wasn’t was all the things we’ve seen in recent games; nervy, disjointed, chaotic and weak. Burn, Schär, Joelinton, Murphy and González in particular looked relaxed, unphased and confident without putting in a 10/10 performance. I’m sure this rubbed off on those around them, and their reward was a couple of well-worked goals, another beauty disallowed, and a clean sheet. You could see the weight lifting off the shoulders of all involved and finishing the weekend in eighth place will make them feel better still. A word for the magnificent Toon Army. I went into town today from my home in the millionaires’ playground of Gateshead. The weather meant that the Metro was banjaxed and they’d stopped buses from going over the Redheugh Bridge in case they ended up on their sides. Yet a battalion of Geordies travelled down to south London (and back again) at the height of the storm, probably in darkness, and they outsang the Crystal Palace faithful when they got there. 10/10 to them. Lukáš Horníček 8 I wasn’t sure he’d be playing, as another poor display may have ended his season. But he was assured, decisive and untroubled, and made a couple of magnificent saves in the swirling wind. Maybe playing behind our more experienced centre backs did the trick but this was a fine display Amar Dedić 8 He looked absolute class in his first few games, then – for me – went off the boil a bit. But this was a cracking performance, energetic, intelligent and focused. As will always be the case, he was out of position once or twice when he charged upfield, but it was those charges that meant he had a hand in both of our goals, including a fine assist for the second. Looks a bargain at £29.5m. Fabian Schär 8 Good to see him back on the pitch. He didn’t have an outstanding game but he just looked assured and unruffled. We’ve missed that. And I’m guessing this had a calming effect on those around him, especially our kee

A much-needed win, deserved if not emphatic. The first half looked like a turgid relegation scrap between two poor teams and I understand that. The weather was foul, neither team had any reason to feel optimistic given recent PL results, and a defeat would have put either team on the ‘clubs-in-crisis’ list. Our manager didn’t do what a lot of fans were hoping and play the majority of the young lads. Instead, he opted for a centre back pairing with a combined age of 68, and a very recognisable midfield and front four. I wouldn’t have gone with a few of those selected but it turned out to be exactly the right call. Newcastle United took control in the second half and won a game that a different XI may well have lost. The performance wasn’t spectacular and it’s only fair to highlight the shortcomings evident in our opponents. But forget what kind of display this was. What it wasn’t was all the things we’ve seen in recent games; nervy, disjointed, chaotic and weak. Burn, Schär, Joelinton, Murphy and González in particular looked relaxed, unphased and confident without putting in a 10/10 performance. I’m sure this rubbed off on those around them, and their reward was a couple of well-worked goals, another beauty disallowed, and a clean sheet. You could see the weight lifting off the shoulders of all involved and finishing the weekend in eighth place will make them feel better still. A word for the magnificent Toon Army. I went into town today from my home in the millionaires’ playground of Gateshead. The weather meant that the Metro was banjaxed and they’d stopped buses from going over the Redheugh Bridge in case they ended up on their sides. Yet a battalion of Geordies travelled down to south London (and back again) at the height of the storm, probably in darkness, and they outsang the Crystal Palace faithful when they got there. 10/10 to them. Lukáš Horníček 8 I wasn’t sure he’d be playing, as another poor display may have ended his season. But he was assured, decisive and untroubled, and made a couple of magnificent saves in the swirling wind. Maybe playing behind our more experienced centre backs did the trick but this was a fine display Amar Dedić 8 He looked absolute class in his first few games, then – for me – went off the boil a bit. But this was a cracking performance, energetic, intelligent and focused. As will always be the case, he was out of position once or twice when he charged upfield, but it was those charges that meant he had a hand in both of our goals, including a fine assist for the second. Looks a bargain at £29.5m. Fabian Schär 8 Good to see him back on the pitch. He didn’t have an outstanding game but he just looked assured and unruffled. We’ve missed that. And I’m guessing this had a calming effect on those around him, especially our keeper and right back. Dan Burn 8 You could pretty much copy and paste what I said about Schär. Just having the big man back gave the whole team a more composed look. He did what he had to do and got in the way of just about everything Palace threw at him. I thought Mateta would be a big threat. In the event, he was rendered impotent. Lewis Hall 7 He’s been the player I’ve marked highest just about every time I’ve done the ratings this season – one of our few bright sparks. But today he was good not great. Took a whack (two in fact) and I think that might have slowed him down a bit. By no means a poor performance but not his best. Nico Gonzàlez 8 At the risk of repeating myself, his was a performance of quiet authority rather than dazzling skills, but that is exactly what was needed. Covered, intercepted, passed and controlled, and was given Player of the Match by the Sky pundit. I wouldn’t argue with that. Joelinton 6 All over the place in the first 20 minutes but slowly got into the game and made the two-man midfield tactic look like it might work. Ran out of steam later in the game and probably should have been subbed off 10 minutes before he was. But he did his job. Jacob Murphy 8 My mate, who has been watching Newcastle United home and away for 35 years, texted me thus: “Murphy was MoM for me….who am I?!”. Like him, I wouldn’t have picked Murph for this fixture, but he justified his selection. Made the correct decision most of the time and played a part in both goals. His cross for the first was absolutely top rank and I also thought his delivery from corners was better than a lot of what we’ve seen this season. He was asked to defend after the subs were introduced, and he did that well, and without complaint. A good day at the office. Joe Willock 6 Another one that wouldn’t have been on my team sheet but no complaints about his showing today. Enthusiastic, committed and energetic. VAR robbed him of a lovely goal but he buzzed around effectively for the 70-odd minutes he was on the pitch. Harvey Barnes 7 Scored a typical Harvey Barnes goal, sweeping a cut back into the net with aplomb. He is probably the best finisher at the club. That aside, he didn’t set Selhurst Park alight, but was solid and industrious. Will Osula 7 I’m not sure he saw much of the ball (not necessarily his fault), but when he did, he looked pretty good. Unlike one or two others who have played the number 9 role this season, he actually looked to get into the box when Murphy and Dedić were attacking down the wing. He got his reward when Murphy found him five yards from goal for a tap in. It’s not rocked science… Newcastle United Players Clapping Away Fans at Crystal Palace Selhurst Park Photo by Simon Ritter via The Mag SUBS Anthony Elanga 5 Fair play to our manager, who was – allegedly – under pressure before this game. He could have brought on defenders and midfielders when subs were needed but he went with Elanga et al instead. That made it difficult for Palace to throw caution to the wind. We got a couple of promising runs out of Elanga; I can see him starting at Everton on Thursday. Yoane Wissa 5 Another positive substitution, he looked sharp and eager when he joined the fray. Should get a run at Everton. Jacob Ramsey 5 Couple of good passes, couple not-so-good. If he’s fit and Jaissle is determined to persist with the two-man midfield gambit, he starts alongside Nico for me. Sean Steur N/A I would have given him a lengthier cameo, but as it turns out, he wasn’t on long enough to judge. Malick Thiaw N/A Came on, got kicked in the head. Went off for a minute. Came back on. Ref blew whistle. Probably wishing he hadn’t bothered. Source

item.title: Florian Wirtz brushes off Jamie Carragher's brutal criticism after starring in Liverpool victory
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-LIVERPOOL-BRIGHTON - AFP Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz has issued a defiant response to the mounting criticism surrounding his performances since joining Liverpool for a club-record fee. The German international, who has struggled to maintain consistency, insists he remains focused on his game despite high-profile pundits questioning his output. Wirtz hits back at punditry pressure The Germany international has found himself under the microscope ever since the Reds committed to a staggering £116.5 million deal to lure him away from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. Despite the pressure of his price tag, the 23-year-old is adamant that he is not listening to the critics who have questioned his output during his time in the Premier League. Wirtz played a pivotal role in the breakthrough against Brighton , as it was his powerful effort that deflected off Pascal Gross to open the scoring. Following that opener, Bradley Barcola provided the assist for Alexander Isak to secure the result. "Maybe I'm just an interesting guy, you know?" Wirtz joked during a post-match interview with the BBC . item.content:encoded: FBL-ENG-PR-LIVERPOOL-BRIGHTON - AFP Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz has issued a defiant response to the mounting criticism surrounding his performances since joining Liverpool for a club-record fee. The German international, who has struggled to maintain consistency, insists he remains focused on his game despite high-profile pundits questioning his output. Wirtz hits back at punditry pressure The Germany international has found himself under the microscope ever since the Reds committed to a staggering £116.5 million deal to lure him away from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. Despite the pressure of his price tag, the 23-year-old is adamant that he is not listening to the critics who have questioned his output during his time in the Premier League. Wirtz played a pivotal role in the breakthrough against Brighton , as it was his powerful effort that deflected off Pascal Gross to open the scoring. Following that opener, Bradley Barcola provided the assist for Alexander Isak to secure the result. "Maybe I'm just an interesting guy, you know?" Wirtz joked during a post-match interview with the BBC . The midfielder, who struggled to find consistent rhythm during his debut year under Arne Slot, appears to be enjoying a new lease of life in the current setup. Wirtz currently boasts a tally of one goal and three assists for the current campaign, figures that he will be looking to improve as he seeks to silence his detractors permanently. "No, I just play my football, and if people want to talk about me or judge me, that's their job. I am not focusing on that. I just want to play football, and more, I cannot do," the playmaker added as he continues to adapt to the rigours of English football. The midfielder hails dominant first-half display Wirtz then praised his team's mindset and commanding start, highlighting their sharp execution in the opening phase of the game. He noted that throughout the first half—particularly during the initial thirty minutes—the squad asserted control by dominating individual duels, generating numerous scoring opportunities, and pairing their attacking tempo with disciplined defending to close out the half securely. "We had the right mentality today to go into this game. In the first half or first 30 minutes, we were on top of them and really good in the duels, creating a lot of chances. It's good to end the half and we defended good. Really happy about that," he explained. "It's really enjoyable. I think many things weren't so good in the last month so I'm even happier that it's going well at the moment. We are in a good way to get where we want to be. We should keep going like that and I'm happy about that." Carragher pulls no punches The most vocal critic of the German star has been Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher, who has repeatedly questioned whether the club received fair value for their money . Following a disappointing loss to Manchester City earlier in the season, Carragher was particularly scathing about the midfielder's contributions to the team. The former defender suggested that Wirtz has had more than enough time to adapt to life in the Premier League. "There is no way Wirtz should be playing ahead of Gravenberch. What Florian Wirtz is doing for Liverpool is not enough right now. He’s played 55, 60 games for Liverpool. He shouldn’t be in the Liverpool team right now. I don’t want to hammer Liverpool players. But we’re not saying this after five-ten games, we’re saying this after 50-60 games," Carragher said. Injury scare at Anfield The victory over Brighton was slightly dampened when Wirtz was forced to leave the field prematurely. After receiving medical attention on the pitch, the midfielder was substituted in the 65th minute, causing immediate concern among the Anfield faithful. The German was eventually replaced by Trey Nyoni as the medical staff began their initial checks on the sidelines during the closing stages of the match. Head coach Andoni Iraola was quick to provide an update on the situation, though he admitted that the congested fixture schedule makes any fitness issue a potential problem. "Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle. It doesn't look very big but we are playing every three days so we need to see where he is," Iraola noted.

item.title: Next Man United manager: Who could replace Michael Carrick?
item.description: Michael Carrick is running out of time to save his job at Manchester United , with the club poised to ramp up the search for a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos took over football operations. Carrick – who impressed during his interim spell in charge last season – has come under huge pressure following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years . That pressure has only intensified after a dismal 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night was followed by a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at home on Sunday, with fans streaming out of Old Trafford in their droves during the second half. While the problems United face run far deeper than the head coach – as highlighted by defender Lisandro Martinez after the defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month – Carrick’s appears to be on the brink following criticism of his tactics by the United captain Bruno Fernandes , who was then left on the bench against Bournemouth. While Carrick remained in charge for Sunday’s defeat to the Cherries , the club have already discussed potential replacements should he follow the departures of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim under the Ineos leadership. Carrick spoke for almost six minutes at the start of his pre-match press conference on Friday, imploring the importance of “sacrifice”, “humility” and “hard work” in an impassioned speech which highlighted the “values” of the club and “respecting” the responsibility of representing United. But who could United turn to as they seek to salvage their campaign? Eddie Howe The Englishman is available after his shock decision to leave Newcastle United in the summer . Howe told the club he needed a break from management but the chance to take charge at Old Trafford, three months later, would surely be too good to turn down if an offer arrives. The 48-year-old remains highly regarded in English football after taking over a Newcastle side in the relegation zone and leading them to the club’s highest Premier League finish in two decades, as well as their first domestic silverware in 70 years. Howe twice took Newcastle into the Champions League playing an energetic, high-intensity style of football that would be popular at Old Trafford. He is currently the favourite with the bookies. item.content:encoded: Michael Carrick is running out of time to save his job at Manchester United , with the club poised to ramp up the search for a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos took over football operations.
