Howe twice took Newcastle into the Champions League playing an energetic, high-intensity style of football that would be popular at Old Trafford. He is currently the favourite with the bookies. Howe led Newcastle to the Carabao Cup in 2025 before leaving at the end of the following season (Getty) Fabian Hurzeler Brighton have been the surprise package in the Premier League this season and the 33-year-old Hurzeler has drawn praise for turning the Seagulls into a side capable of competing with the country’s biggest clubs. Brighton’s 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal earlier this season was a masterclass in modern coaching while Hurzeler’s side also knocked United out of the Carabao Cup with a brilliant 3-2 win at Old Trafford. The Independent’s Chief Football Writer Miguel Delaney has reported that Hurzeler is admired at Old Trafford but Brighton would demand significant compensation for the highly-rated German and United may not have the cash. At Brighton, Hurzeler has also enjoyed an environment where the club have made all the right decisions off the pitch. At United, he would arguably be walking into the opposite. The Brighton boss said on Friday : “I’m fully focused on my job here. I’ve got no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days. I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and the job he has done at Manchester United the last season. He's a great human being, a great personality, and I really respect him. There's nothing more to say about that. I’m really privileged to be here. I’m part of a journey [at Brighton] and I still have this feeling when I go to bed that we are not finished with our journey... “We have built this [together] over the years. We’ve had good periods, we’ve had bad periods. To build these connections you need time. You don’t take these things for granted. It’s a people business. Making a people business out of this pressure business is something I don’t take for granted and something I won’t throw away that fast.” Fabian Hurzeler led Brighton to a brilliant win at Old Trafford earlier this season (Getty) Julian Nagelsmann The former wunderkind of German coaching was reportedly on United’s radar when they sacked Ruben Amorim at the start of the year, but as an option for the summer following the World Cup. Well, that was a bit of a disaster for the former Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig coach, as Germany were knocked out in the last-32 by Paraguay. Nagelsmann, 39, would naturally be interested in managing United and the club’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, previously worked with him at Red Bull. Julian Nagelsmann has been considered by United in the past and is available (Getty) Unai Emery The Spaniard has done a superb job at Aston Villa by securing Champions League qualification and ending the club’s trophy drought with victory in the Europa League. But Aston Villa will be even more determined to keep Emery given the club are only in the early stages of their rebuild under him, having completely overhauled the spine of their team over the summer. As it is, Emery enjoys complete control over his project at Villa Park, a reality he is unlikely to find at Old Trafford, while he appears enthused by the challenge of constructing a second competitive team in the Premier League. With Emery, who is under contract until 2029, United would also need to pay Villa compensation, and that may place him above their budget. Unai Emery appears enthused by the challenge of building ‘Villa 2.0’ (Getty) Antonio Conte The appeal of the combustible Italian only has grown while United have been accused of becoming too passive and pedestrian on the pitch. Conte is one of the most demanding coaches in the game and would instantly bring a level of intensity and urgency that has been lacking this season, while his CV – with Serie A titles at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli and a Premier League crown with Chelsea – commands respect. Conte also brought an immediate improvement when he took charge of a floundering Tottenham five years ago and led them back into the Champions League, which now has to be United’s biggest concern. So the 57-year-old offers impact, but then what? Conte has a sharp tongue and is not afraid to criticise his bosses if he feels they are failing to support him. His exit from Tottenham in March 2023 followed a stunning evisceration of the club in a now legendary press conference at Southampton. United would be playing with fire but options of Conte’s calibre are few and far between. In a statement on Friday, Conte distanced himself from the Manchester United job while branding reports that he is in “advanced negotiations” with any club as “speculation”. He said: “Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right. I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my ‘strong personality’. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.” United could be playing with fire if they turn to Conte (AFP/Getty) Cesc Fabregas The former Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea midfielder is developing a reputation as Europe’s brightest young coach – as his brilliant Como side demonstrated by thrashing United in the Champions League on Wednesday night. The Spaniard appears committed to his project in northern Italy, though, and also has a financial incentive to continue leading Como in their debut Champions League campaign due to owning a stake in the Serie A club. The 39-year-old’s own stock is also rising and the lure of returning to one of his former clubs in the future, such

item.title: Micah Parsons snaps at NFL’s officiating after Packers’ three-point loss vs. Lions
item.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Micah Parsons has taken aim at NFL officials after the Green Bay Packers suffered a narrow 20-17 defeat to the Detroit Lions, with a controversial roughing the passer penalty becoming a major talking point. The Lions secured victory with a last-second field goal from Jake Bates, but the officiating attracted plenty of attention following two disputed penalties against Green Bay. Parsons was watching from the sidelines as he continues to recover from a torn ACL, but that did not stop the Packers’ pass rusher from making his feelings clear on social media. Micah Parsons questions NFL’s roughing the passer calls Parsons shared his frustration on X, tagging both the NFL and its officiating account after officials penalised Packers defensive lineman Karl Brooks for roughing the passer late in the fourth quarter. He wrote: “@NFL, @NFLOfficiating let’s just go to flag football if every time a QB gets touched it’s roughing the passer!” The call came after Brooks made contact with Lions quarterback Jared Goff following an 18-yard completion to tight end Sam LaPorta. The 15-yard penalty helped Detroit continue its drive before Bates delivered the winning field goal. Former NFL quarterback Tom Brady also questioned the decision while working as a Fox Sports analyst. “My goodness. What is that?” Brady said during the broadcast. “There’s no way!” Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino also backed the criticism, saying: “That’s teach-tape tackle. That’s not roughing the passer.” It was not the only disputed decision, with Packers defender Brenton Cox Jr. also penalised for roughing Goff earlier in the contest. Parsons could face a fine for publicly criticising the officiating, according to reports, although no punishment had been confirmed. A suspension is considered unlikely. Green Bay also had opportunities to win the game, with two missed field goals from Trey Smack and a crucial fourth-quarter interception thrown by Jordan Love contributing to the defeat. Parsons has now missed seven consecutive games while recovering from his ACL injury, leaving the Packers to wait for his return as the debate over the officials’ decisions continues. item.title: Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: Mbappé brace wins El Clásico for Los Blacos
item.description: Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: Mbappé brace wins El Clásico for Los Blacos Real Madrid won the season’s first El Clásico on Sunday night, thanks to a brace from Kylian Mbappé. The Frenchman put Real ahead shortly before half-time, but Raphinha levelled for Barça on the hour mark. The match looked to be heading for a draw until Mbappé netted a late winner, causing José Mourinho to kneeslide on the touchline. As it happened Hans-Dieter Flick made two changes to his Barcelona side after their 4-2 loss to PSG on Tuesday night, with Rodri and Fermín López replacing Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal in midfield. Meanwhile, José Mourinho named four changes, with Andriy Lunin, Ibrahima Konaté, Marc Cucurella and Yan Diomande replacing Thibaut Courtois, Antonio Rüdiger, Álvaro Carreras and Vinicius Junior. Barcelona dominated large parts of the first half, with Anthony Gordon forcing three saves out of Lunin, and plenty of other chances going begging for the hosts. The opener came in the 41st minute, when Mbappé arguably got incredibly lucky. It was Diomande’s delivery into the box that initially seemed to be dealt with by Gerard Martín; however, the Barça defender could only clear it into the leg of the onrushing striker, who saw the ball bounce into the back of the net off his shin. Diomande came close himself minutes later, breaking in behind the Barcelona defence before firing his shot into the side netting, meaning the score stayed at 1-0 going into the break. The first real chance of the second half saw Raphinha draw the hosts level when his left-footed strike from inside the area found its way past Lunin after a clever disguised pass from Pedri. Arda Güler looked to put Madrid back ahead mere moments later, but Joan García was on hand to palm his shot away from danger. Lunin made a spectacular save in the 65th minute, when he managed to react quickly and keep out Martín’s close-range header. The winning goal came in the 87th minute, when Los Blancos broke away down the left following some superb skill from Jude Bellingham in the middle of the park. The Englishman laid it off to Eduardo Camavinga, who played a nice one-two with Cucurella before setting up Mbappé to tap home from close range and earn Mourinho’s side all three points at the Nou Camp.

item.title: Canelo Álvarez Arrives in Riyadh; Mexico vs The World Card Proceeds
item.description: What to Know Fighters on the “Mexico vs the World” card in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, have begun safely arriving in preparation for the event scheduled on Saturday, October 31 The fight card headlined by Canelo Álvarez vs Christian Mbilli is still scheduled and apparently going forward while violent attacks continue in Saudi Arabia and the Middle East. Fight Week events begin on Wednesday, October 28, with grand arrivals. Despite continued security concerns due to political unrest and violence targeting Saudi Arabia, fighters have begun arriving in Riyadh in advance of the “Mexico vs the World” fight card scheduled on Saturday, October 31, with Fight Week activities scheduled to kick off on Wednesday. WBC World Super Middleweight Christian Mbilli of Quebec will make his first title defense against former undisputed super middleweight champion Saul “Canelo” Álvarez of Mexico. The card, titled “Mexico vs the World,” also featured matchups between top Mexican champions and contenders with opponents from around the world. On Sunday night, DAZN Boxing as well as Turki Alalshikh, chairman of the General Entertainment Authority, posted video of Álvarez arriving in Riyadh alongside former undisputed world heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk. Álvarez and several of his stablemates have been training at Usyk’s gym located in Valencia, Spain. IT’S GO TIME!! Canelo has touched down 🔥✈️ 🎥 via: Canelo 🎟️ Buy #CaneloMbilli NOW at https://t.co/yxybEeoyF5 | Oct 31 | Mexico vs The World | @ringmagazine 🤳 https://t.co/wjbUKav4gW — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 26, 2026 Also arriving with Team Canelo was WBO World Featherweight champion Rafael “Divino” Espinoza, also training in Spain. Although he wasn’t pictured, WBA World Super Middleweight champion Jaime Munguia of Tijuana likely made the trip as well. Álvarez has insisted for weeks he would fight in Riyadh without regard to any concerns about safety. On his arrival, Canelo said, “I love to be here in Riyadh, and I’m excited to fight on Saturday, so I can be a world champion again.” Mbilli and his stablemate with Eye of the Tiger Management also on the card, super lightweight Arthur Biyarslanov, arrived several days ago, although they reportedly took an alternative route to the Saudi capital. Eye of the Tiger president Camille Estephan confirmed he would travel on Monday to support his fighters. Je pars lundi et j’arriverai mardi en Arabie Saoudite, l’équipe est déjà là. Dans mes bagages, Il y aura évidemment le drapeau du Québec. Je connais Christian je sais ce qu’il a sacrifié pour arriver jusqu’ici et surtout à quel point il est déterminé à gagner ce combat. La semaine passée, il a dit: “Même si ça va avoir lieu en Arabie Saoudite, vous pouvez me croire que je vais défendre ma ceinture pour Montréal et le Québec en tapant Canelo le 31 octobre.” Toute l’équipe a fait le travail nécessaire pour lui donner les meilleures chances de réussir. Both he and Delgado expressed serious concerns about the conditions involved in making the trip. While in San Antonio, Texas, working the corner of Albert Gonzalez Saturday night, Garcia spoke with reporter Francisco Salazar about the situation . He acknowledged that his fighter Delgado would still want to show up, “because fighters fight.” But from his perspective as Delgado’s trainer, Garcia pointed out that even if he and Delgado left from California for Riyadh on Monday, they would be routed through an airport out of harm’s way, then drive for several hours to Riyadh, arriving on Tuesday at the earliest. They would end up with just two days to get acclimated, prepare for the fight, and for Delgado to make weight. Robert Garcia Explains His Dilemma “We’re a week away from the fight in Saudi. It’s on the other side of the world. They never sent us any flights. They still haven’t sent us any flights,” said Garcia on Saturday night. “I’ve been there multiple times … The first three or four days, you’re walking around like a zombie. We’re falling asleep in the middle of the day. It’s tough. Right now, if we were to leave tomorrow … it’s already Monday in Saudi. It takes a day to get there. They’re going to take us to another airport. We’re going to drive five hours, six hours. We’re going to get there Tuesday. They’re only going to give me Wednesday and Thursday to make weight? To get used to the time change, It’s impossible. “If we would have had our flights a week ago and said we didn’t want to go, that would be different. But we were always ready,” said Garcia. He said with Delgado’s opponent already in Riyadh for several days, it sets up an unfair situation. New Opponent for Divino Espinoza Rafael Espinoza arrives in Riyadh on Sunday evening. Photo: Courtesy X/Turki Alalshikh In another schedule change, the Middle East Professional Boxing Commission which officially oversees combat sports in Riyadh, declined to authorize Lorenzo Parra of Venezuela (24-1-1, 18 KOs) as an opponent for WBO World Featherweight champion Rafael “Divino” Espinoza of Guadalajara (28-0, 24 KOs) . WBO President Gustavo Olivieri announced on Friday, October 24, that Ricardo Blandon of Nicaragua (21-6, 14 KOs) will step in as a replacement opponent. No reason has been given why Parra, the WBO number one contender, was not sanctioned for the fight. Blandon, age 34, is a super featherweight who has never fought outside Central America with no notable opponents save a loss to former champion Rene Alvardo in 2024. However, he fought at 115 pounds as recently as 2022, and at 5-foot-8, he’ll give up only five inches to the 6-foot-1 Espinoza. Featherweight David Picasso of Mexico and super featherweight Reito Tsusumi of Japan have confirmed their safe arrival in Riyadh for their undercard fights. Fight Week Schedule for Mexico vs the World Turki Alalshikh of the Saudi General Entertainment Authority posted the Mexico vs the World Fight Week schedule on Wednesday. All fighters on the card make their first public appearance as the grand arrivals kick off Fight Week events on Wednesday, October 28. The fight pre-fight news conference takes place on Thursday, October 29, and will air live on DAZN Boxing at 2 p.m. ET/11 a.m. PT (9 p.m. in Riyadh. Weigh-ins are scheduled on Friday, October 30, also airing live on DAZN Boxing at 2 p.m. ET/11 a.m. PT. Ongoing Safety Alerts Remain in Place The U.S. State Department is maintaining its travel advisories for the Middle East, including a Level 3: Reconsider Travel advisory for Saudi Arabia including conflict escalation, flight cancellations, and airspace closures. On Oct. 23, all U.S. non-essential government personnel were ordered to return to the U.S. from the region. A Level 3 alert is labeled “Reconsider Travel” and covers Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Isreal, and the West Bank. Details here . The State Department cites active threats from Iranian drone and missile targeting along with attacks and threats from Houthi rebels in Yemen directed at Saudi territory, infrastructure, and American interests. item.title: Texas Senator Ted Cruz’s appearance at United States GP podium ceremony leads to loud boos from fans
item.description: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Texas Senator and Chief of the Senate Commerce Committee Ted Cruz appeared on the podium for Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix in Austin. Cruz has been an elected member of the United States Senate from Texas since 2013, but likely did not get the reception he expected when he appeared on the podium to hand out the trophies to the top-three drivers at the 2026 U.S. GP. As Cruz handed trophies to Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc, and Kimi Antonelli, the crowd at Austin let their feelings on their elected Senator know. Ted Cruz receives heavy boos at Formula 1 appearance in Texas As Cruz appeared on the F1 podium stage, the crowd very audibly started booing, even continuing the boos when race-winner Antonelli lifted up the trophy handed to him by Cruz. F1 commentator James Crofty acknowledged the boos on the broadcast as well. “People are already voting with their voice.” Cruz is not up for election in 2026, but has endorsed Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in his race against the Democratic nominee James Talarico. The last election Cruz ran in was the 2024 race for the Class I Senate seat in Texas, winning over Democratic nominee Colin Alfred. Notably, Austin, where the 2026 United States GP was held, gave 70% of its votes to Alfred in that race, with Cruz receiving just 27.16% of the popular vote in the city. He has previously been unpopular in Austin, so it should not be surprising to see the fans here react this way to Cruz. Cruz’s appearance at the 2026 U.S. GP is not a rare occurrence for an American politician. Most notably, Donald Trump attended the 2024 Miami Grand Prix, albeit before winning the 2024 U.S. Presidential election. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has attended multiple Miami Grand Prix events since the race’s addition to the F1 calendar in 2024. Texas Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick also attended the U.S. GP in Austin. item.title: Knicks make unfortunate NBA history not seen from defending champion in 15 years
item.description: Knicks make unfortunate NBA history not seen from defending champion in 15 years originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Defending NBA champions tend to have targets on their backs at the start of the season. Every squad in the league wants to batter down the group that hoisted the Larry O'Brien trophy just a season prior. The New York Knicks , led by Jalen Brunson, are no different. In fact, after their 111-102 loss against the Orlando Magic , they joined the 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks on the wrong side of NBA history. This unfortunate feat has not been seen in the association for a little over 15 years. Knicks join Mavericks in unfortunately historic NBA feat after loss to Magic The Knicks did everything in their power to beat the Magic. Jalen Brunson and Co. popped off in the first half. In the first quarter, they scored 28 points while allowing the Magic only 21. The Knicks followed up with a second-quarter slip, scoring only 24 points while the Magic got 27. All was seemingly going according to plan for the Knicks and Brunson. By the third quarter, the two squads tied the quarter with 23 points apiece. Then, a collapse of absolutely historic proportions happened. The Magic rallied to score 40 points in the fourth quarter. The Knicks? They only got 27 points. In the end, the Knicks lost 111-102 to the Magic. This is now their third-straight loss to start the 2026-27 NBA season. They got smothered by the 76ers in a 106-100 heartbreak, followed by a 107-103 clutch beating by the Boston Celtics . The Knicks are now the first defending champions to start their campaign with a 0-3 record since 2011-12. Dirk Nowitzki and the Mavericks were the last team to do the same, per ESPN Insights. So, what does this mean for the Knicks? Historically speaking, the fates are not on their side. See, the era of parity in the NBA is at an all-time high, and there is no incentive to tank given the contract pressures of Josh Hart and Karl-Anthony Towns. They will also have a rough schedule. Their next games have them facing the Detroit Pistons , Chicago Bulls , Philadelphia 76ers, Brooklyn Nets , Milwaukee Bucks , and Cleveland Cavaliers . Three of those teams could be easy wins, but changes need to happen for that to happen. Compared side by side with the 2011-12 Mavericks, things don't look great for Brunson and the Knicks . That squad managed only 36 wins, though it was a lockout-shortened season with just 66 games. Eventually, this Mavericks squad would come crashing down in the first round against the season runners-up, the Oklahoma City Thunder, led by Kevin Durant, James Harden, and Russell Westbrook. There is no monolith archetype of defending champion in the NBA. The Knicks can stray away from these comparisons to the Nowitzki-led Mavericks. However, it will take a lot of willpower to do so. Will the magic of New York save them again for a repeat, or was that all just reserved for the summer o

item.title: Ballon d'Or 2026: Who are the leading contenders?
item.description: Ballon d'Or 2026: Who are the leading contenders? The Ballon d'Or race is rarely decided by numbers alone. Club silverware, individual brilliance and performances on the international stage can all shape the vote, with the balance between them often proving decisive. The 2026 race has produced a fascinating collection of contenders. Harry Kane has enjoyed a prolific season at Bayern Munich , Kylian Mbappé has continued to rewrite goalscoring records, and Lionel Messi has shown he remains capable of delivering on the biggest stage. Meanwhile, Rodri , Lamine Yamal and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia all have compelling cases of their own. But with major trophies won and individual records broken, who has done enough to claim football's most prestigious individual honour on Monday night? Rodri Team trophies: FA Cup, League Cup, FIFA World Cup. Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Golden Ball Rodri knows what it takes to win the Ballon d'Or, having claimed the award in 2024 after an outstanding season for Manchester City and Spain. Another World Cup triumph has strengthened his case for a second victory. The Spain captain was named Player of the Tournament as La Roja lifted the trophy, recognition of his influence on the biggest stage. His biggest obstacle is the club campaign. While the World Cup Golden Ball is a major point in his favour, a less successful season at club level leaves him with ground to make up on rivals who combined individual brilliance with domestic and European silverware. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia Team trophies: Ligue 1, UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup Individual awards: UEFA Champions League Player of the Season The Georgian was in devastating form as Paris Saint-Germain made it back-to-back Champions League wins in 2025/26. Kvaratskhelia scored 10 goals and created six more in 16 European appearances for the Champions League winners, and added nine more goals across all competitions. Georgia's absence from the World Cup hurts his chances, with major tournaments often decisive in Ballon d'Or votes. Lionel Messi Team trophies: MLS Cup, Campeones Cup Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Silver Ball, FIFA World Cup Silver Boot, MLS Golden Boot, MLS Most Valuable Player A record-extending ninth Ballon d'Or looked a real possibility for Lionel Messi as Argentina reached a second straight World Cup final, but defeat to Spain has reduced his chances. The Ballon d'Or race is crowded with players who have enjoyed exceptional seasons in Europe. Messi's achievements are remarkable, but the strength of the opposition means another victory would require a particularly persuasive argument. Messi, however, was magnificent in North America, showing that even at 39 he remains one of the game's greatest talents. Kylian Mbappe Team trophies: None Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Golden Boot, FIFA World Cup Bronze Ball, UEFA Champions League Top Scorer, Pichichi Trophy Kylian Mbappe has argued the Ballon d'Or is an individual accolade that shouldn't be decide

Club silverware, individual brilliance and performances on the international stage can all shape the vote, with the balance between them often proving decisive. The 2026 race has produced a fascinating collection of contenders. Harry Kane has enjoyed a prolific season at Bayern Munich , Kylian Mbappé has continued to rewrite goalscoring records, and Lionel Messi has shown he remains capable of delivering on the biggest stage. Meanwhile, Rodri , Lamine Yamal and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia all have compelling cases of their own. But with major trophies won and individual records broken, who has done enough to claim football's most prestigious individual honour on Monday night? Rodri Team trophies: FA Cup, League Cup, FIFA World Cup. Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Golden Ball Rodri knows what it takes to win the Ballon d'Or, having claimed the award in 2024 after an outstanding season for Manchester City and Spain. Another World Cup triumph has strengthened his case for a second victory. The Spain captain was named Player of the Tournament as La Roja lifted the trophy, recognition of his influence on the biggest stage. His biggest obstacle is the club campaign. While the World Cup Golden Ball is a major point in his favour, a less successful season at club level leaves him with ground to make up on rivals who combined individual brilliance with domestic and European silverware. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia Team trophies: Ligue 1, UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup Individual awards: UEFA Champions League Player of the Season The Georgian was in devastating form as Paris Saint-Germain made it back-to-back Champions League wins in 2025/26. Kvaratskhelia scored 10 goals and created six more in 16 European appearances for the Champions League winners, and added nine more goals across all competitions. Georgia's absence from the World Cup hurts his chances, with major tournaments often decisive in Ballon d'Or votes. Lionel Messi Team trophies: MLS Cup, Campeones Cup Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Silver Ball, FIFA World Cup Silver Boot, MLS Golden Boot, MLS Most Valuable Player A record-extending ninth Ballon d'Or looked a real possibility for Lionel Messi as Argentina reached a second straight World Cup final, but defeat to Spain has reduced his chances. The Ballon d'Or race is crowded with players who have enjoyed exceptional seasons in Europe. Messi's achievements are remarkable, but the strength of the opposition means another victory would require a particularly persuasive argument. Messi, however, was magnificent in North America, showing that even at 39 he remains one of the game's greatest talents. Kylian Mbappe Team trophies: None Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Golden Boot, FIFA World Cup Bronze Ball, UEFA Champions League Top Scorer, Pichichi Trophy Kylian Mbappe has argued the Ballon d'Or is an individual accolade that shouldn't be decided by team success. Real Madrid and France both fell short in the big tournaments, despite Mbappe's brilliance. The leading scorer in La Liga, the Champions League, and World Cup, Mbappe made his mark on the major events. His 10-goal World Cup campaign saw him shatter the all-time goal record and become the first multi-Golden Boot winner. The absence of major team trophies is the obvious drawback. Ballon d'Or voters have often favoured players who combine individual excellence with collective success, and Mbappé cannot point to a Champions League or World Cup winner's medal this time. But if the award is genuinely about the best individual player of the year, Mbappé has an argument few can match. Lamine Yamal Team trophies: La Liga, Supercopa de España, FIFA World Cup Individual awards: La Liga Player of the Season, Zarra trophy Lamine Yamal seems destined for Ballon d'Or success at some stage, after a runners-up finish last year. At 19, he would become the youngest-ever winner, following a sensational season that delivered La Liga and World Cup success. He scored 16 goals and assisted 11 more during Barcelona 's title win, but failed to have a major impact - despite success - for Spain in the summer. He scored just once in eight games during an injury-impacted World Cup. Harry Kane Team trophies: Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, German Super Cup Individual awards: Bundesliga top scorer, European Golden Shoe Harry Kane might have the most well-rounded argument of any contender. The Bayern Munich striker scored 61 goals in 51 games as his side secured a domestic treble, while his scoring record earned him the European Golden Shoe. Few players can match that combination of individual production and team success. While England failed to end their tournament drought, Kane's six goals helped the Three Lions to a third-place finish at the World Cup. It represents England's best-ever performance on foreign soil. Michael Olise Team trophies: Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, German Super Cup Individual awards: Bundesliga Player of the Season Olise outperformed club teammate Kane to win the Bundesliga's Player of the Season award. The winger scored 15 league goals and provided 19 assists, while he was named in the Team of the Tournament for the Bundesliga, Champions League, and FIFA World Cup. Olise has the numbers to enter the conversation, but he may need a stronger individual narrative to turn an excellent season into a Ballon d'Or-winning one.

item.title: Toyota’s new GR GT3 to make early debut in Japan next month
item.description: Motorsport photo The new Toyota GR GT3 will make its competition debut in Japan next month ahead of a wider rollout in 2027. Rookie Racing, a team owned by Toyota chairman Akio Toyoda, will enter the Japanese marque’s next-generation GT3 car at the SUPER GT finale at Motegi on 7-8 November. The GR GT3 will replace the squad’s regular #32 Mercedes-AMG GT3 in the GT3 division and will compete as an ‘open’ entry, making it ineligible for points. Two-time Super Formula champion Hiroaki Ishiura and 19-year-old Tokiya Suzuki have been named as its drivers for the double header. The car will run on Bridgestone tyres, despite Dunlop being selected as the sole supplier for the GT300 class next year when SUPER GT’s long-running tyre comes to an end. Toyota has been developing a GT3 contender under its own brand name for several years, having first shown an early preview of the car at the Tokyo Auto Salon back in 2022. In July 2025, the GR GT3 made its public debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed, with Haas Formula 1 driver Esteban Ocon driving it up the famous hillclimb. The Japanese manufacturer brought the car back to Goodwood this year, with its World Rally Championship driver Elfyn Evans among those taking it for a spin. Esteban Ocon, TOYOTA GT Concept Esteban Ocon, TOYOTA GT Concept Toyota had been mulling over entering the car at selected races in 2026, with the Nurburgring 24 Hours initially viewed as the ideal race for the car’s competition debut. However, that plan did not materialise, but the Japanese marque remained keen on giving its new GT3 racer an outing before the end of the year. The GR GT3 will be made available to customers starting next year, when it will replace the ageing Lexus RC F GT3. While manufacturers typically limit the availability of new GT3 cars to select teams in the first season, the GR GT3 will certainly race in the World Endurance Championship’s LMGT3 division in the hands of the ASP team. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
item.description: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby. Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher. item.description: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. item.dc:creator: Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.content:encoded: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
item.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more. Try our other sports emails: as well as the occasionally funny football email The Fiver from Monday to Friday, there are weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown , and our seven-day roundup of the best of our sports journalism in The Recap . Living in Australia? Try the Guardian Australia’s daily sports newsletter Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Recap newsletter: our free sport highlights email
item.description: The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Subscribe to get our editors’ pick of the Guardian’s award-winning sport coverage. We’ll email you the stand-out features and interviews, insightful analysis and highlights from the archive, plus films, podcasts, galleries and more – all arriving in your inbox at every Friday lunchtime. And we’ll set you up for the weekend and let you know our live coverage plans so you’ll be ahead of the game. Here’s what you can expect from us. Try our other sports emails: there’s daily football news and gossip in The Fiver , and weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown . Living in Australia? Try the Guardian Australia’s daily sports newsletter Continue reading...
